## Windows Network Location Awareness

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009jYrfzCAC/windows-network-location-awareness
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-05-04T08:00:04.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

mryan

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited by Ben_Garrison June 30, 2023 at 1:47 PM

Windows Network Location Awareness

Microsoft Windows Network Location Awareness (NLA) functions to detect when on a public/private/domain network. Windows Defender Firewall implements different firewall rules depending on the network location. Generally, a less restrictive policy applies on the Domain, and unless the machine detects the Domain profile all AD functions (GPO/Kerberos/etc) will not function.

Therefore, it's important that NLA service functions correctly to detect the Domain. Recently I've seen customers change the default action for Public/Private networks to be DENY, which further restricts this functionality.

Therefore, this article describes what rules to create in Defender firewall to allow NLA to function with Zscaler Private Access.

This

article describes the base firewall rules necessary for Zscaler Client Connector to function, and to connect to the Zero Trust Exchange.

ZCC will connect to the Zero Trust Exchange and ZCC will intercept traffic based on the application segmentation policy. In general, an App Segment will exist for Active Directory consisting of a wildcard (for DNS) and the FQDNs (for the domain controllers).

When NLA triggers, it causes Windows to perform the Netlogon process. This consists of the DNS lookup (Which will be intercepted by ZCC/ZPA) and returns the IP addresses of the domain controllers. NLA will then attempt to connect to the domain controllers and authenticate - therefore detecting the Domain, and moving to the Domain network profile.

The key processes here are NLASVC, NetLogon, and LSASS. Therefore creating firewall rules appropriate for this is necessary.

In MSDefender Firewall create rules for the following

Program %systemroot%\system32\lsass.exe

Service - Network Location Awareness

Service - Netlogon

These should be permitted access to the IP range 100.64.0.0/16 or 100.64.1.0/24 if you need to be more restrictive (Active Directory DNS would be one of the first processes Windows will query for, so generally it will result in an IP address in the first 255 of the subnet range).

It may further be possible to restrict this to the appropriate TCP/UDP ports used for AD Discovery of TCP/88, UDP/88, TCP/389, UDP/389, TCP/445.

Once the rules have been created, create a registry entry

HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NlaSvc\Parameters

Add a DWORD parameter :AlwaysExpectDomainController

Set value to:1

This triggers NLA to poll for the domain controller more frequetly.

Once this is done, Windows will poll for the domain controller on network change, or after ZCC starts, which will then be permitted by the Windows firewall. ZCC can then intercept the traffic and pass through ZTE to the domain. The success of this flow will result in the Domain profile becoming active.

You can run the following in powershell to trigger the network status change -

Get-NetAdaptor -physical | Restart-NetAdaptor

You can run the following in powershell to identify the network profile currently applied -

Get-NetConnectionProfile

Video is available

here

to explain this functionality.

This

help article from Microsoft covers the registry entries which can effect how NLA functions

ZPA - Forwarding

Ben_Garrison

Embedded video to make it easier.

mryan

(Employee)

3 years ago

To make it a bit easier - here is the registry entries needed.  This also sets the firewall rules for LSASS, NLA, and NetLogon.

This restricts public/private profile to access AD (through ZPA) to the 100.64.1.0/28 range (specifically small since AD will be in the first 16 IP's returned by ZPA) on TCP/UDP 389 necessary for Windows NLA to detect the domain and move to domain profile.

Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NlaSvc\Parameters]

"AlwaysExpectDomainController"=dword:00000001

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SharedAccess\Parameters\FirewallPolicy\FirewallRules]

"{7C042967-B092-4198-B538-F4ACA02B587C}"="v2.30|Action=Allow|Active=TRUE|Dir=Out|App=%ProgramFiles%

\\Zscaler\\ZSATray\\ZSATray.exe

|Name=ZCC-ZSATray|"

"{71227982-7F1F-4CD9-88FE-6D1BBFBE74D5}"="v2.30|Action=Allow|Active=TRUE|Dir=Out|App=%ProgramFiles%

\\Zscaler\\ZSATrayManager\\ZSATrayManager.exe

Dmills488

(Customer)

3 years ago

We are also running in to this problem.

With ZPA up Windows now thinks that the local adapter is DomainAuthenticated, Defender then applies its Domain policy to that adapter. The Domain policy is wide open both ways as it's intended to be used on a trusted network like a full-tunnel VPN or enterprise LAN.

In this state with the local adapter having the Domain policy applied it now allows all inbound/outbound connectivity from an untrusted network.

## Dynamic Latency-Based Service Edge Assignment (ZIA)

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009lJ5qWCAS/dynamic-latencybased-service-edge-assignment-zia
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-01T19:21:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

jalomari

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited July 6, 2023 at 2:33 PM

Dynamic Latency-Based Service Edge Assignment (ZIA)

In this article, we will help you to test the latency-based service edge assignment (ZIA) feature. Before we start with the steps it is important to understand the problem that this feature is resolving. Improving the end users experience is a crucial goal that Zscaler has been committing to providing. After many companies started adapting work from anywhere and hybrid work environments (i.e., home and office), and because users have different network environments at home, it became essential to implement an intelligence method into the Client Connector to allow choosing the best service edge with the lowest latency. This enhancement can substantially improve the end user experience and reduce the administrator’s workload by minimizing the number of support tickets.

Client Connector connects users to the service edge that is configured in the PAC file. Administrators can manually add the ZIA public service edge to the PAC file, or use $ {GATEWAY} and $ {SECONDARY_GATEWAY} Zscaler specific variables to connect users based on geo-proximity. Prior to Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) 4.2, ZCC would failover to the secondary service edge, if and only if the primary service edge becomes unreachable. In other words, if the tunnel to the primary is up and the user experiences a latency issue with that DC, the ZCC won’t failover to the secondary DC that can offer a better performance. To overcome this limitation, a new feature was added into Client Connector 4.2 where a constant HTTP-based probing to the primary and the secondary service edges is conducted. ZCC utilizes Time to first byte (TTFB) to compare the latency between both service edges and then based on the following parameters: Probe Interval Threshold, and Probe Sample Size the failover may occur. Zscaler supports this feature with all traffic forwarding methods; Tunnel with Local proxy, Tunnel 1.0, and Tunnel 2.0. In tunnel 1.0, Client Connector utilizes HTTP CONNECT to the public service edge for 407 (Proxy Authentication) response to calculate the latency. In Tunnel 2.0, Client Connector utilizes HTTP GET to http://gateway.[cloud].net /generate_204 response to calculate the latency (As shown in the below pic)

To test the feature:

To start testing, you need a tool that can be used to simulate high latency and packet loss. In this article we will use Clumsy tool to add extra overhead.

After downloading Clumsy, run the .exe file

Enable Dynamic ZIA service edge assignment under forwarding profile and decrease the values to simulate a faster failover.

Enable and set a high values for: Lag, Drop and Throttle checkboxes. For ip.DstAddr, add the primary DC VIP (You can get this value from ZCC GUI)

Once the criteria are met, the failover will occur. As you can seen in the below screenshot, the Server IP was changed from 104.129.194.38 to 104.129.192.254.

End user will be notified.

To investigate issues related to dynamic service edge latency-based assignment, you can use ZSATunnel.log files to get more insight (keywords: Changing active T2 instance based on latency, LBZ).

Client Connector

Mark_League

(Employee)

3 years ago

What kind of network is the user on?  Look in the Mobile Portal (from ZPA console, on the left click "Client Connector").  In the portal go to Administration | Forwarding Profile.  Review the forwarding profile that is applied to this user, and their network conditions at the bottom of the profile "Forwarding Profile Action for ZPA".  See screenshot.

In this example, when Client Connector detects users on VPN or Off of my Trusted Network, ZPA enables.  However, when they connect to my trusted network, the service disables and there is no option for the user to enable it.  To allow this on Trusted Network, I just toggle "On Trusted Network" to "Tunnel".  Then, in Client Connector, you can go to More | Update Policy to immediately update the setting.  Otherwise, Client Connector will update on it's next polling interval ( I think that this is usually an hour or two, if I recall correctly).

Let me know if this helps,

Mark

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009nNtCmCAK/zpa-partner-login","lastmod":"2023-07-23T22:00:49.000Z","id":"0D54u00009nNtCmCAK"} -->
## ZPA partner login

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009nNtCmCAK/zpa-partner-login
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-07-23T22:00:49.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Authentication

Bob_Pants

(Customer) asked a question.

July 20, 2023 at 10:25 PM

ZPA partner login

My organization is not a ZPA customer, however one of our client is, and they are asking us to enable ZPA partner login in our tenant, the expectation is that doing so will enable our ZCC users to be able to access the 3rd party origanizations apps published via ZPA.

I am getting conflicting information on whether this will work or not from Zscaler, could someone pls let me know what exactly enabling ZPA partner login does, the documentation does not have a lot of info on this, and whether this would provide the access to another Zscaler customer apps that does have ZPA

Thanks

ZPA - Authentication

2 answers

1.82K views

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

3 years ago

Yes this will work.   You do not have to be a ZPA customer to allow your users to access a partner ZPA tenant.  You do not have to have ZPA licensing for this, the owner of the "partner" tenant does.  If you do become a ZPA customer, the feature lets your users easily switch between your ZPA tenant and the partner tenant or tenants.  The owner of the partner tenant keeps control their own access policy, how your users authenticate into their tenant, etc.

The ZPA and Client Connector partner login feature effectively lets you either:

1) log in to additional secondary ZPA tenants on a Client Connector already registered to a primary ZIA and/or ZPA tenant

2)  allow a partner (aka third party) who has a Client Connector registered to their own primary ZIA/ZPA tenant to add your ZPA tenant as a secondary tenant.

In your case, it sounds like

You are a ZIA customer presumably, but not yet a ZPA customer.

You have a client  that is a ZPA customer.

Your users need to access some private applications in the client's data center

Those applications are not published via ZPA's clientless Browser-based Access.

If you ask support to enable partner logins in your Zscaler Client Connector portal, you will see a new administration item appear called "ZPA Partner Logins".  In that menu there are two options.  "Allow Partner Logins to This Tenant" (not relevant to you.) and "Allow Users of This Tenant to Login to Other Tenants" (this is the one you want).  Note that your users need to be on Client Connector v4.1 or later.

Your users will on their next policy update see a Private Access icon appear in their Client Connector application even though you do not have ZPA.  Within that there will be a link for "+ Add Partner Tenant".

When your user clicks that link they will be prompted to enter the username or email assigned to them by the partner for their Identity Provider.  There are many possibilities for how that's handled on their end.

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited August 11, 2023 at 8:14 PM

Citrix Workspace via Browser Access

Has anyone successfully deployed Citrix Workspace via Browser Access? We have everything in place, and can access the initial login, but when we get logged into the Citrix Gateway there seems to be an issue with the handoff to Workspace and it wants us to log into Workspace even though that is not the behavior it exhibits when on network or when connecting via ZCC, Gateway seems to basically be a Proxy and SSO type deal and takes you straight into Workspace. Upon trying to authenticate to Workspace when prompted, we get an error stating that "Your logon has expired. Please log on again to continue." And that is an endless loop.

Just wanted to ask around before we started getting other groups and vendors involved. Thanks for any insight or advice!

ZPA - Browser Access

1 answer

1.52K views

avshch

likes this.

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hey,

I have not tried this personally, and this information is a little old. But from what I understand this can work but there are some prerequisites

Browser access can sometimes reuse TCP sessions, which needs to be disabled on the backend. Your Zscaler account team can help facilitate this. Please contact them and have them refer to SET-300

The citrix receiver will need to be configured to run everything over 443 and with FQDN

Again, not sure if this info is still valid, but worth a shot. If not, ZPA browser access has been expanded to Clientless Access, which supports Web and RDP, SSH and VNC connections in the browser. That could be another option depending on what you are using citrix for.

ozanogur

(Partner)

3 years ago

Hello, yes I have opened the ticket, and the problem was:

When you have an existing PRA portal, and when these new features like screen recording, and credetials are enabled then the CNAME is changed( "pra" added), this change needs to be reflected in the DNS record :

old CNAME   record : xxxxxxxxxxx..

p.zpa-app.net

new CNAME record: xxxxxxxxxxx.

pra

p.zpa-app.net

2 answers

akita_down

(Customer)

3 years ago

The first thing you need to ensure is that your app connector is resolving the application to a private IP. If the app connector DNS resolution is public, it will redirect to the CNAME that is configured for browser access.

If that is confirmed correctly, then it sounds like there's some forwarding issues on the client.

I would suggest creating 2 separate access policies. One for ZCC users where the access type is ZCC and a separate policy where Browser access is only allowed to a different group of users. This would be a good test to understand how the traffic is being forwarded.

## ZPA Terraform Provider - v3.0.0-beta (September, 19 2023)

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009zdiqiCAA/zpa-terraform-provider-v300beta-september-19-2023
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-09-19T21:21:25.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

wguilherme

(Employee) asked a question.

September 19, 2023 at 9:21 PM

ZPA Terraform Provider - v3.0.0-beta (September, 19 2023)

Enhancements

PR #355

- Introduced the new resource and datasource zpa_microtenant_controller

PR #355

- Added support to the new Microtenant Controller feature to the following resources:

zpa_app_connector_controller,, zpa_app_connector_group, zpa_application_segment, zpa_application_segment_browser_access, zpa_application_segment_inspection, zpa_application_segment_pra, zpa_application_server, zpa_policy_type, zpa_policy_access_rule, zpa_policy_access_forwarding_rule, zpa_policy_access_timeout_rule, zpa_policy_access_inspection_rule, zpa_policy_access_isolation_rule, zpa_segment_group, zpa_server_group, zpa_provisioning_key, zpa_machine_group, zpa_service_edge_group, zpa_service_edge_controller

Important:

The new attribute microtenant_id is optional. The provider also supports the microtenant ID configuration via the environment variable

ZPA_MICROTENANT_ID

which is the recommended method.

Important:

This feature is in limited availability and requires additional license. To learn more, contact your local account team.

PR #356

- Added support to the following new ZPA Cloud Browser Isolation resources and datasources:

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_banner - Cloud Browser Isolation Banner Controller

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_certificate - Cloud Browser Isolation Certificate Controller

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_external_profile - Cloud Browser Isolation External Profile Controller

Data Sources

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_banner - Cloud Browser Isolation Banner Controller

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_certificate - Cloud Browser Isolation Certificate Controller

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_external_profile - Cloud Browser Isolation External Profile Controller

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_region - Cloud Browser Isolation Regions

zpa_cloud_browser_isolation_zpa_profile - Cloud Browser Isolation ZPA Profile

Important:

Cloud Browser Isolation (CBI) is a licensed feature flag. Please contact your local account team for details.

PR #363

- Added support for COUNTRY_CODE object type within the zpa_policy_access_rule resource. The provider validates the use of proper 2 letter country codes

ISO3166 By Alpha2Code

Issue #361

PR #366

- Added

ISO3166 By Alpha2Code

for country_code validation on zpa_app_connector_groups and zpa_service_edge_group resources

ZPA PSE Terraform Azure

Dear Community,

I am trying to deploy PSEs to Azure via Terraform, I have compared the Terraform code between AWS and Azure. As a requirement, we should have an inbound rule to the PSEs from the ZCCs to allow the connectivity. I see such an ingress rule in the SG module in the AWS code but for the Azure NSG, I don't see the incoming 443 rule.

Am I missing something?

Regards

G-Man8

Hi Rallis,

Zscaler Support took me though this once but in short, you are looking for your 'Diagnostic' tab, add Filter then select username as 'ZPA LSS Client'.

You should see the IP configured in your log receiver along with the unique ports for each receiver type.

Hope this steers you in the right direction

(Customer) asked a question.

December 6, 2023 at 10:19 PM

App Connector in Azure VM with Hub and spoke architecture

Hi,

We are planning on setting up ZScaler ZPA connector in Azure. I have some questions with regards to best practice as I'm fairly new with this product.

1) Do you create a dedicated subnet for the VMs? If yes, any required subnet size

2) Do you leave the default NSGs and leave it up to the connector to control inbound and outbound.

3) Any concerns implementing the app connector in the hub subnet with a hub and spoke architecture?

Cloud Connector

2 answers

694 views

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

3 years ago

So the app connector needs to be able to see the applications it is going to serve up.   So for this part you'll need to make sure you do not have any NSGs that will interfere with that.

The app connector needs to have outbound access on 443 to the zpa cloud at a minimum.

I personally recommend associating a dedicated IP to the machine in case you ever want to do ip anchoring in the future.

D4rkie

(Customer)

Hi,

dedicated subnet not required. Size depends on sizing demands. We use vmss as well

Nsg Config we locked down inbound Completely except management like ssh from bastion snmp from monitoring etc

Outbound we have ip any any to be able to reach everything in the whole network

We have own nat gateway from appconnector to internet to not put the load on central egress vnet and to have specific out found ip for sipa independent of the amount of app connectors

## Secure DNS preventing users from working with ZPA

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ADFrCsCQL/secure-dns-preventing-users-from-working-with-zpa
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-01-11T13:41:08.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

Johnb

(Customer) asked a question.

December 14, 2023 at 5:11 PM

Secure DNS preventing users from working with ZPA

HI. We are new to Zscaler ZPA and just started using it recently. We ran into an issue that is concerning with Secure DNS. If a user winds up with a DNS server that support secure DNS, such as Googles 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4, the browsers are now defaulting to use Secure DNS. This basically breaks Zscaler ZPA from intercepting the URL's for our internal servers and the traffic does not come through the ZPA connectors. The workaround is to disable Secure DNS in the browser, but this does not seem to be a good long term solution. Is anyone else running into this, and does anyone know if Zscaler is working towards a better solution to handle clients using Secure DNS other than needing to have each user disable Secure DNS in their browsers?

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

3 answers

1.75K views

G-Man8

likes this.

G-Man8

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi John,

Very good question and thanks for raising this !

Get your company to back to ER-7997.

I asked Zscaler support anyway which replied with the ER and statement below:

Interoperability considerations for DNS over HTTPS (DOH) and ZPA.

This note highlights interoperability considerations for DNS over HTTPS (DOH) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA).

There are two ways in which end users can access internal applications using ZPA - Zscaler App & Browser Access

Access to internal applications using Zscaler App:

When a browser originates a DNS request for internal applications, ZApp intercepts the DNS request and responds with an IP address in the Carrier Grade NAT (100.64.x.x) address space. Hence the ability to correctly identify DNS requests is key for ZApp to forward application requests to ZPA.

What is the implication for ZPA?

While Firefox and Chrome have announced plans to support DOH, they have also implemented extensive fallback mechanisms for situations where DoH may not be successful. DOH is expected to fail, when a browser attempts to resolve an internal application for which there is no entry in public DNS. In this scenario, the browser will simply fall back to the traditional approach for resolving DNS, at which point, ZApp will successfully intercept DNS requests.

However, one scenario to note, is when a browser is able to successfully resolve DNS for an internal application, because there is also a public instance of this application. While such a scenario is less common, it does occur. In this case, DOH requests from the browser for this application will be successful and ZApp will be unable to intercept DNS requests. The workaround is to disable DOH as the default method for originating DNS requests in the browser.

Is there a performance impact?

A browser that resorts to DOH by default, will first attempt DNS resolution using DOH and then fall back to traditional DNS resolution i.e send DNS request on port 53. The fall back may contribute additional milliseconds to the eventual successful DNS response, depending on how quickly the browser detects DOH failure and attempts a traditional DNS request. However, the additional milliseconds are not expected to result in a noticeable delay towards the end user.

Access to internal applications using Browser Access:

When accessing applications via Browser Access, ZPA relies on the web browser to resolve the application using public DNS. So for this scenario, ZPA should not have any issues with browsers that leverage DOH.

## ZPA APP connector support for RHEL v9

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AFRKLvCQP/zpa-app-connector-support-for-rhel-v9
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-01-22T00:37:34.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Cloud Connector

Dave-Bourke

(Partner) asked a question.

January 10, 2024 at 5:15 PM

ZPA APP connector support for RHEL v9

Do we know when ZPA APP Connector will support for RHEL v9 ?

I can't see anything on the community and the documentation only mentions v7 and v8

Regards

DABk

Cloud Connector

5 answers

1.72K views

Top Rated Answers

Dylan Merida

(Employee)

2 years ago

Hi Dave,

RHEL 9 will be available in late Q2 CY24 for pre-built images and RPM. Zscaler will be providing Red Hat licensing in the pre-built images to ease the burden and deployment logistics on our customers. Also note, Docker currently only supports CentOS 7, not any form of EL9 yet.

As for migration, it's straightforward and involves deploying new app connector VMs with new provisioning keys and groups. They are then staged for regional off-hours deployment into existing server groups. There will be more shared on migration through TAM and SE soon.

We realize the release is close to the June 30th CentOS 7 end of maintenance, making it difficult to thoroughly test and fully migrate in time. In light of this, we will continue to support the CentOS 7 / EL7 binary until Dec 24, 2024.

Customers will remain responsible for the operating system and security vulnerabilities (as-is established with the shared responsibility model in licensing and agreements today) However, we have evaluated the risk to be very low due to the following unique aspects of our architecture:

Our binaries for AC and PSE use statically-linked security libraries that are updated independently from the OS (like openssl-fips);

The OS has no third-party listeners;

The image is based on CentOS 7 minimal with little to no extra packages installed;

SSH is disabled by default; and

PSE has only a single listening service on TCP 443 using the same statically-linked binary as mentioned above.

It's also likely that any major RCE-level vulnerability, such as with the OS-packaged OpenSSL, DNS client, and Kernel modules, will be rapidly patched by Red Hat and the CentOS foundation for the at least the next year. This has been observed in the past with other operating systems due a large install base / market share remaining after end of maintenance.

If you have any further questions, please reach out to me or your TAM / support resources.

Warm regards,

Dylan Merida

Sr Product Manager - App Connector

ZPA PM

PSE has only a single listening service on TCP 443 using the same statically-linked binary as mentioned above.

It's also likely that any major RCE-level vulnerability, such as with the OS-packaged OpenSSL, DNS client, and Kernel modules, will be rapidly patched by Red Hat and the CentOS foundation for the at least the next year. This has been observed in the past with other operating systems due a large install base / market share remaining after end of maintenance.

If you have any further questions, please reach out to me or your TAM / support resources.

Warm regards,

Dylan Merida

Sr Product Manager - App Connector

ZPA PM

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited February 13, 2024 at 4:26 PM

Hybrid Autopilot DJ with ZPA  windows pre-logon

Hello guys, I m setting up a hybrid domain join autopilot, this ia 90% done, is working the objects are created in both AAD and AD. The only thing is missing is the Zscaler prelogon screen.

we are using zscaler with device tunel in our environment, but I do need this to be activated before the first user log on. I see the zscaler installed during the ESP but I cannot see the “Zscaler Diagnostics” after the device setup is finished. We need this so the user not be obliged to be in the office in order to be able to logon the the PC. Does zscaler support this feature? Basically I need that the ZPA to activate and connect the to domain network before the first very logon. Thank you.

ZPA - Authentication

9 answers

797 views

Logan_Miller

(Employee)

2 years ago

By default, the  Machine Tunnel only gets established when the authentication to ZCC is completed and the user accessing the App Profile with the Machine Tunnel configuration. That's why you see the "Zscaler Diagnostics" after the device setup initially...

To overcome this, you will want to use the "POLICYTOKEN" flag when installing ZCC. This will allow you to pull the App Profile Configuration and establish the Machine Tunnel on device setup. You can find some more information at the link below!

https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/customizing-zscaler-client-connector-install-options-msi

G-Man8

No, PolicyToken is just a unique key that relates to which App Profile Policy the Zscaler client should load BEFORE a user logs into ZCC.

In our case we call 'Zscaler Machine Tunnel Enrolment' App Profile.

The Machine token is the key element required to enroll your Machine Tunnel, without it you'll never get the Diagnostic Tab.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

2 years ago

You can,

App connector for publish applications within the DC, or public cloud. So that we users can access the private application within the DC /private cloud

Cloud connector is user for outbound connections from cloud workload to internet and internal applications.

So short answer is both are needed if you need to ZIA and ZPA.

## ZPA Private Service Edges in Scaling Group.  What happens to traffic when a Member of the the group scales in..

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AM2te1CQB/zpa-private-service-edges-in-scaling-group-what-happens-to-traffic-when-a-member-of-the-the-group-scales-in
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-03-04T15:41:46.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

mrpackethead

(Customer) asked a question.

March 2, 2024 at 10:15 PM

ZPA Private Service Edges in Scaling Group.  What happens to traffic when a Member of the the group scales in..

I am planning on deploying Private Service Edges, which will be part of a scaling group, so we can have an appropriate amount of resources running to match demand, which changes widely over the day.

If one of my private edge servers is shutdown, what happens to traffic flows that are using that edge? Do they just fail, and the client re-establishes connectivitity to another of the service edges? Does that result in a noticable impact to the end users?

Is there a way of signalling to Zscaler, that this node is marked for shutdown so that all traffic can be gracefully drained away, before shutdown?

ZPA - Forwarding

1 answer

326 views

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

I am looking at some documentation and from what I can tell, if the service edge is shut down, the traffic flows using that edge would be disrupted.  The private edge doesn't have a persistent local database and all the service configurations are kept only in memory, unable to recover the data once it's shut down.

The traffic would need to be redirected to a Public Edge or another Private Edge. If the private Edge cannot communicate with a public edge, it will fail.

As for graceful handling of this, I believe this can be handled with a redirect process. If I understand correctly, the private edge "publishes" their addresses to the cloud, and these are included in the redirection message.  If you use the "publicly access" flag for private edge, then the address  is included in the redirection message, whether the client connector appears on the same network or not.  This tells me that traffic can be redirected to a Public Edge before the Private Edge is shutdown.

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/forwarding-traffic-virtual-service-edges

## ZPA New Application Setup

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ANByXFCQ1/zpa-new-application-setup
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-03-11T09:11:34.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

jitendrasingh

(Partner) asked a question.

March 11, 2024 at 6:44 AM

ZPA New Application Setup

Scenario 2 - A new office is being brought online, which will use the existing location like A, Connectors & PSEs. What would you check to ensure that ZPA has been setup correctly for the new site?

Scenario 2 – A user is trying to access an application and is not working. Assuming it is an issue with ZPA, what troubleshooting steps would you run through ?

Scenario 3 – New application is onboarded into location A, what is required and how would you set this application up in Zscaler ?

Client Connector

2 answers

323 views

G-Man8

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hi,

My 2 cents on the subject :)

Scenario 1 - Depends but I would start by trying to access a basic application to ensure the ZPA session is going via the expected PSE's (Public or Private) and App Connectors for location A without any lag.

Scenario 2 - Does the same application fail in location A, if not then either the local App Connectors dont have the required routing or a Firewall is blocking it. Use the 'Support Information' tab to 'TCP_Ping' to the destination and port from the assigned App Connectors.

Scenario 3 - Depends on the Application, is it mainly client to server initiated traffic ?

Has the Application been micro-segmented so your App Connectors dont have rights due to network segment ? Do you still have a Wildcard Discovery segment to catch these 'new' applications ? Has the Application owner provided all the required FQDN's and ports ?

We've seen several Applications still configured to use IP's rather than FQDN.

Hope this helps but also curious on other people's view :)

You have two courses basically.

## ZPA DNS Timeouts and other questionable behavior

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ARPI2bCQH/zpa-dns-timeouts-and-other-questionable-behavior
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-07-01T19:36:48.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

mcdonamw_ews

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited April 23, 2024 at 9:49 PM

ZPA DNS Timeouts and other questionable behavior

My company just started using Zscaler and we're having DNS issues that seem bizarre to me. I have performed significant analysis using packet captures, including the one built into ZCC itself, but I don't fully understand what I'm seeing as things just aren't adding up how I would expect.

Let me start by saying I found another old post that pretty much sums up exact issue, which is regarding timeouts during DNS queries. That can be found here:

https://community.zscaler.com/Zenith/s/question/0D54u00009evlEeCAI/problem-with-zscaler-dns-hijacking-advanced

Short summary of the above post: DNS lookups result in timeouts when using NSLookup and not adding a trailing dot at the end of the fqdn. Sometimes multiple timeouts but ultimately resolving the query.

I understand NSLookup treats anything without the trailing dot as unqualified, so the pc then goes about tacking on its dns suffixes as part of the query. What I don't understand is the behavior of where those queries are sent to be resolved.

Say

my domain dns suffix is example.net

and

Zscaler is configured to route *.example.net across the internal tunnel.

When I submit a query for '

host1.example.net'

(no trailing dot)

, the packet captures show the request goes out as '

host1.example.net.example.net.'.

That part I expect. What I don't expect is that query is attempted to be resolved by external DNS resolvers. Note: this domain does exist externally as we're using split-brain dns.

Eventually the query for the intended hostname resolves internally as expected. Additionally submitting

'host1.example.net.'

(with the trailing dot)

, it resolves instantly and all traffic remains internal.

In short: Why would '

host1.example.net.example.net.

' attempt to resolve externally, at all? While the host is malformed due to dns suffix addition, it is ultimately still on the example.net domain, which should remain internal. I would expect all queries for this domain to remain internal while ZCC is connected.

Secondly, I've noticed resolving simple netbios names fail entirely the first time (not timeout), but subsequent retries fine. I'm sure it's cached somewhere from that point forward but I don't understand the first time failure.

I'm hoping someone with advanced knowledge here of ZPA can help me out.

Note: I'm not sure what community 'topic' this would fall under. I see nothing for DNS specifically.

ZPA - Forwarding

5 answers

1.89K views

CKAIJA

(Employee)

2 years ago

Okay so to be clear ----on what I am understanding as your Question ----- your issue is with DNS lookups across ZPA timing out or not being handled appropriately at the ZCC client.

Keep in mind troubleshooting --- this is two different transactions ------ ZCC to Broker/CA ----- and (internal services) to APP conn --- outbound to BROKER  -------

Synthetic IPs are client ZCC facing only  --- RFC 6598 --- 100.64.0.0/10 ... these are used for proper routing client side only  --- As the ZPA Ztunnel serves as a transparent traffic redirect for each application opened in turn

So let's break this down shall we ------ ZCC - with ZPA enabled --- what version ?

Next your AV and Firewall are allowing the prerequisites out  your getting connected to the service and authenticated.

You have configured an APP connector in your DC that is leveraging a Wild Card *.

example.net

and the ports you have allowed it to use are the following

I am hoping you have a defined APP segment that is just TCP port 1 -- pointed at AD servers outside the wild card yes?

Wildcard/ Discovery segment

TCP   --- 2  to 52

TCP  ---  54 - 65535

Yes

and you set this to an access policy that allows for your particular user to access this Application segment

Now --- if all things are equal ---- When your ZCC client fires up  --- the connection side you care about is CLIENT to BROKER ------ aka hash segment matched and a synthetic IP was created to ensure the traffic goes to the ZTunnel for ZPA as configured at Start up of the Client

Connection 1 will be to our CA's and then a Broker  --- this ensures access and latest "HASHED" app segment delivery to client

Connection 2 as this is a hash based lookup and DNS is not sent to ZPA ---- the Client OS is running ZPA above the Network Interface Card -- so layers 3  and 4  do not matter to ZPA --- only parts of layers 5 most of  6 and some of 7 ----

Because your OS is constantly looking at the hashes delivered to it from the BROKER / CAs for a Match and when a MATCH is seen ---- it creates a SYNTHETHIC IP --- to route the traffic at the lower layers below  5 of the OSI model functions  (3 & 4)

So at this point what are you seeing ---- as PING -a -t and tracert  should both start working but on the client you will see a 100.64.0.0 address ---- never your internal IPs ---

So what do you see

CKAIJA

(Employee)

2 years ago

There is also an assumption here your APP conns are configured with the correct local DNS servers and search domains and NTP settings --- to work 100% in your environment --- I would leave 1 of our as a back up if all else fails -- and as to the time back ---

time.nist.gov

is a good one or one of the preconfigured server pools

Also in the ZPA tenet you configured  DNS search domains on the action drop down or button on the top right

mcdonamw_ews

(Customer)

2 years ago

I can't answer a lot of your questions as the ZScaler configuration is managed by another team.  In this particular case, I'm just a user (even though I'm part of the IT team testing it).  I'm aware of the synthetic IP functionality, but I'm not concerned about IPs.

With that said, I believe everything is configured properly.  DNS is working, but it's behaving wonky under certain conditions.  At any rate, I'll try to clarify the issue in its most simplistic terms.

When using NSLookup, if you do not specify a period at the end of the fqdn, it's treated as a host, not an fqdn, even if the domain is specified.  When this happens the computer tacks on its DNS suffix(es) before sending out the query.

It doesn't matter if it's an actual external domain vs internal domain.  Internal hosts end up with a double suffix  E.g.,

NSLookup

www.yahoo.com

becomes

www.yahoo.com.mydomain.net

NSLookup

host.mydomain.net

becomes

host.mydomain.net.mydomain.net

The above queries seem to end up going out to external DNS servers, whereas they should stay internal given their suffix of

mydomain.net

(problem #1)

These external queries

timeout

several times, but then return a proper result.

(problem #2)

Note:

when all those suffix-based queries fail (those hosts do not exist), the PC sends the initial query as it was entered (without suffix), which is where the true answer comes from.

If I fully qualify the query by adding a period at the end, the suffix is not added and lookups are instantaneous (no timeouts).

NSLookup

www.yahoo.com

(<-period) stays

www.yahoo.com

and hits external DNS servers.

NSLookup

host.mydomain.net

(<- period) stays

host.mydomain.net

and hits internal DNS servers.

New finding:

if I fully qualify those mangled fqdns above, e.g.,

host.mydomain.net.mydomain.net

(<- period), the request

still

goes external.  What???

(Problem #3)

It all boils down to this, ignoring all the nonsense with NSLookup;

Why would

host.mydomain.net.mydomain.net

attempt to resolve by external DNS servers, whereas

host.mydomain.net

stays internal?  They are both on

*.

mydomain.net

and thus should be considered internal, (regardless of the suffix being listed twice).

Why are external queries causing timeouts at all?  This doesn't happen when off zscaler network.

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

There might not be enough information here to really help isolate. This could be happening from any number of viewpoints examples being:

High Packet loss or network connection

Frequent TCP retransmits or frequent TCP selective ACK's

Application firewall or some other IDS terminating long running SSL/TLS connections

DHCP lease renewal process experiencing issues.

The client, broker or network could also be playing a part. For instance, if the problem happens on a home network but not a public wifi, then it's likely not a broker issue and something that is with the client, home network or ISP.

If you have ZDX, you can maybe run some reports, or use the new AI tool to help troubleshoot. If not, I would suggest getting with support so they can help you isolate.

Maybe someone has some real world experience with this issue and can have you turn some knobs and see if something changes! I will watch the thread

- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

JoeE

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited May 6, 2024 at 4:36 PM

Selective ZIA/ZPA forwarding based on internally resolved IP Address

We have Azure Private Endpoints on domains such as *.windows.net that resolve to private IPs within our data center, but Microsoft also has public endpoints on that domain for general use. Would there be any way to selectively route traffic to hosts on the .windows.net domain to ZPA ONLY if the host resolves to a private IP within our data center? To date we have been adding the FQDN of the Private Endpoint hosts to Application Segments in ZPA, but with the volume of new Private Endpoints being created this is becoming difficult. So we are looking for any solution that would allow us to send traffic to *.windows.net over ZPA, but ONLY if that resolves to a private IP within our data center.

ZPA - Forwarding

2 answers

708 views

mathias

(Partner)

2 years ago

Hi JoeE,

I don't know if this would be useful in your case, but what about using a DNS Gateway?

It worked under the following conditions.

​Create an APP segment for an IP address in ZPA

Prepare a DNS server  that resolves

servicebus.windows.net

(sample) to 10.255.255.243 (sample) and allow access from Zscaler's global IP.

Register the global IP address of your DNS server in ZIA's DNS Gateway settings.

If your DNS is under NAPT, write static NAT rules. you don't know from which address of Zscaler the DNS query will come, so allow all future data centers.

​​Write redirection rules to DNS gateways in ZIA's DNS Control

Fig1 shows a PC with ZCC installed accessing

servicebus.windows.net

to the 10.255.255.243 Fortigate provided on-prem.

Notes.

It seems that it is not possible to write criteria like specific FQDN groups in DNS Control, i.e. split DNS, so all DNS queries that fly here will be forwarded on-prem.

To prevent this, it is necessary to narrow down the domain in advance with Domain Inclusion in ZCC or, in the case of GRE/IPsec, a forwarder on-prem (not related to the destination to be flown by DNS control).

As a matter of fact, it is puzzling how this mechanism can be accessed by the ZPA.

​I thought that the order of operation of ZCC is that ZPA first determines whether the FQDN or IP is registered in the App segment, and if it is not there, it is sent to ZIA.

Therefore, I thought that even if I registered only an IP address, ZPA would not be used unless I hit the IP address with a browser.

This time, by using a DNS gateway, this assumption may have been broken.

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

2 years ago

I've the same problem.

Best i could come up with so far is to create a app segment like *.

database.windows.net

So

foo.database.windows.net

gets sent 'into ZPA'.

Then it depends on how the connector resolves the FQDN - either it resolves it to our internal IP -> traffic gets sent to the private azure instance

or it resolves to a public IP -> traffic gets sent back through GRE to ZIA and from there to Azure public instance.

For some cases have another app segment, say

bar.database.windows.net

which is set for 'bypass zpa'

FQDNs in that segment are directly sent to ZIA instead of long client->ZPA cloud->ZPA connector->GRE->ZIA->Azure path.

Far from ideal but without better regex support for app segments (like acme*.

database.windows.net

) the best i could find.

(Partner) asked a question.

Trusted Network selection criteria

Hi

I'd like to know if there's a selection criteria to choose a trusted netwok before another when a user matches conditions for several networks.

I mean, considering that I have defined 3 trusted networks:

TN A -> condition= DNS server A. Only suitable for users on site A

TN B -> condition= DNS server B. On ly suitable for users on site B

TN C -> condition= DNS search domain. For users on any other site (but users on site A and B also match this condition)

And I also have deployed Private Service Edges for ZPA on site A and B, and associated the Trusted Network A with the Private Service Edge A, and the Trusted Network B with the Private Service Edge B

For me it seems clear that users from a site diferent than A or B will match the Trusted Network C due to their DNS Search Domain and set the ZPA broker to any of the Private Service Edges based on geolocation, but what happens with users on sites A and B?

I want that users on site A set their ZPA broker to Private Service Edge on site A as they match the Trusted Network A, but they also match the Trusted Network C condition. How can I know what trusted network will these users consider being when they match conditions from more than one?

Thanks. Regards

Client Connector

Hi @Jesus Molina​ ,

I'm not aware of a selection criteria other than 'any' or 'all' but would you environment allow 'HOSTNAME AND RESOLVED IP ' ?

We use 'HOSTNAME AND RESOLVED IP' along with DNS server + DNS Suffix to assign 'Trusted Network' but as you have 3 sites it does get somewhat challenging. Our DNS has been configured so it's only resolves to the expected IP for selected locations.

Have you considered looking into the

new

ZCC 4.4 which adds additional options like Network Range , Default Gateway or DHCP server ?

Maybe worth checking if Zscaler already has an ER that meets your requirements ?

User16182582818315999266

(Customer) asked a question.

July 5, 2024 at 9:21 PM

Remote Tanium PXE Boot Server with ZPA allowing local ports to pass.

We are currently trying to architect a remote solution for our organization to have a 3rd party vendor image new devices for us using Tanium PXE boot. We have installed ZPA on this server and have created a forwarding bypass rule for the PXE port 66-69 and 4011. When they initiate the process it fails. When ZPA is off its works up until the point it needs to grab the offline domain join file (ODJ). Which is understandable. Anyone ever successfully accomplish this before?

ZPA - Forwarding

6 answers

450 views

Top Rated Answers

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

2 years ago

Assuming that it's a ServerOS (e.g. Windows Server), then this is not a supported configuration.  Client Connector is not supported on Servers.

Since I think you said you're bypassing PXE from it anyway, removing client connector should resolve the Tanium and PXE issues.

Then for any ZIA/ZPA Zscaler for Workloads issues I recommend working with your Account Team SE and TAM, if you have one, to determine what the best option is for your workload needs (e.g. cloud connector, branch connector, network tunnels, etc).

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AXQvvfCQD/privilige-remote-access
- Type: Q&A

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

Peiman

(Customer) asked a question.

July 9, 2024 at 11:12 PM

Privilige Remote Access

Hello Community,

I configured PRA, and I followed the instructions step by step. My PRA portal is reachable from outside of the trusted network, but after authentication, none of the defined application segments show up in the portal for the end user. I just get a blank page. Any idea what part is the culprit?

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

3 answers

687 views

kevin.kiele

likes this.

kevin.kiele

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hi Peiman,

To actually see servers/workstations on the PRA portal after authentication, you must configure "Privileged Console" (Resource Management > Privileged Remote Access > Privileged Consoles). Click on "Add Console", select the portal that you configured, and select the PRA application(s).

Then click "Next" and configure the console as you want (name, protocol, etc.). Make sure the option "Display on console" is enabled. This ensures the console button shows up on the PRA portal.

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any other questions regarding PRA.

Kind regards,

Kevin Kiele.

iamolivasmith

2 years ago

Hi,

I have faced the same consider before. So you need to make sure that there are no network or firewall settings blocking access to the application segments. You must verify that the PRA portal has the necessary permissions to communicate with the defined application segments.

Thanks

## Howto import ZPA App Connector VMware OVA into Proxmox

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AZExkKCQT/howto-import-zpa-app-connector-vmware-ova-into-proxmox
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-07-29T05:01:11.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Admin Portal

Nelson

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited July 25, 2024 at 8:14 AM

Howto import ZPA App Connector VMware OVA into Proxmox

Zscaler recently released updated ZPA App Connector images in OVA format. Which are great if your running VMWare. But I'm running Proxmox in a lab environment. How do you get these OVA images imported into Promox? Let me show you in 5 steps.

1. Import OVA into Proxmox

First step is to place a copy of the 'zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.ova' file onto your Proxmox host using SCP. Once there, you will need to unpackage the OVA file(which is simply a TAR file) with the following command: "tar -xvf zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.ova". This will unpackage the OVA file and provide the following 3 files:

zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05-disk1.vmdk

zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.mf

zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.ovf

From here, we need to ask Proxmox to read the OVF file and import the disk and host settings. We can do this with the 'qm' command and the following syntax:

qm importovf zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.ovf

An example of what this looks like in my lab is this:

# qm importovf 104 zpa-connector-el9-2024.06.05.ovf bay3-lvm

Logical volume "vm-104-disk-0" created.

transferred 0.0 B of 64.0 GiB (0.00%)

transferred 655.4 MiB of 64.0 GiB (1.00%)

...

transferred 64.0 GiB of 64.0 GiB (100.00%)

2. Assigning Network interface

Unfortunately, Proxmox can't convert the OVF file perfectly and we need to tell it about the new network. interface we want to use. We can do that with the following command (change the command to suit your host ID and network bridge):

# qm set 104 --net0 virtio,bridge=vmbr0

update VM 104: -net0 virtio,bridge=vmbr0

3. Assigning SCSI card

We also need to tell Proxmox about the SCSI hardware that this VM is using. I'm using a vmware emulated pvscsi card that seems to work well for this host:

# qm set 104 --scsihw pvscsi

update VM 104: -scsihw pvscsi

4. Assign CPU Architecture

Next, I need to tell Proxmox about my CPU architecture, x86-64. You can do that with this command:

# qm set 104 --cpu cputype=x86-64-v2-AES

update VM 104: -cpu cputype=x86-64-v2-AES

5. And now you should be able to start the VM we just imported and log in

ZPA - Admin Portal

## Zscaler ZPA Access Functionality

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AcZmhFCQS/zscaler-zpa-access-functionality
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-04T13:40:06.000Z

ZPA - Forwarding

azizislam

(Partner) asked a question.

Edited September 27, 2024 at 2:23 AM

Zscaler ZPA Access Functionality

Please clarify the following for me regarding Zscaler ZPA access and functionality for Cisco SDWAN with Zscaler security umbrella?

For any access (from any sites) which need to go to datacenters (for retrieval of any data from servers hosted in those datacenters), will the Zscaler Edge Node just “route” that flow to the firewall positioned in that datacenter?

Or will any security processing be done in the Zscaler cloud for that specific flow? I would assume none, as it would entail double processing for security on that flow increasing transmission delay!!!

Will there be any case(s) where flows will just be “routed” by the Zscaler Cloud to the datacenter FW’s (and not security processed)?

Also, for user-to-server traffic and server-to-server traffic how would this traffic routing be any different?

Would highly appreciate if someone could clarify this access functionality (or provide reference to a document that clarifies this issue).

Thanks very much.

ZPA - Forwarding

3 answers

332 views

Rachit Gupta

likes this.

zywong

(Partner)

2 years ago

The traffic flow will be Client --> Zscaler Private Service Edge --[Seek for the available App Connector]--> App Connector (Selected) --[DNS Lookup if its FQDN to your local DNS Umbrella i assume?]--> Application / Server the user want to access to for data retrieval

The policy enforcement for the user's access will be determine on what you configured in your access policy (ZPA Portal)

Your Firewall is the gateway for your DC's perimeter, if the outbound connectivity for your App connector is block there is no way it will be reachable, but of cause if your outbound connectivity is allowed, the session for the user will be established through the App connector to the desired application. Just remember there is no inbound connectivity towards Zscaler to your hosted App Connector to access anything within your infrastructure. It is always an outbound connectivity TLS1.2

User-to-Server as explained at #3, Server to Server adopts the same but your probably need Branch/Cloud Connectors as an additional with some tweak in network configuration to adopt full Zero Trust architecture for your server to server or app to app communication. (Suggest to reach out to Zscaler's AM/SE to discuss this further)

Hope it helps, cheers!

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

2 years ago

For any access (from any sites) which need to go to datacenters (for retrieval of any data from servers hosted in those datacenters), will the Zscaler Edge Node just “route” that flow to the firewall positioned in that datacenter?

Zscaler dont have any role If Branch to DC communication through SDWAN overlay. If there are App connectors installed in DC and branch users using ZCC or browser access, then routing to be through user - ZPA- App connector in DC.

Or will any security processing be done in the Zscaler cloud for that specific flow? I would assume none, as it would entail double processing for security on that flow increasing transmission delay!!!

Leverage Policies in ZPA module If the traffic goes through Zscaler Private access. Continuous policy  and posture checks will happen at ZPA end for each communication.

Will there be any case(s) where flows will just be “routed” by the Zscaler Cloud to the datacenter FW’s (and not security processed)?

All traffic will be allowed through access control policies and inspection policies in ZPA to internal applications.

App connector makes outbound communications and no inbound connection.

Also, for user-to-server traffic and server-to-server traffic how would this traffic routing be any different?

ZCC / browser access / branch connector can use for user to server communications. You need to leverage cloud connectors and branch connectors for server-to-server communication.

## ESXi mgmnt console access through Zscaler SSE cloud

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AcpLP6CQM/esxi-mgmnt-console-access-through-zscaler-sse-cloud
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-08T13:52:26.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Geetanjali.geetanjali

(Partner) asked a question.

October 3, 2024 at 2:25 PM

ESXi mgmnt console access through Zscaler SSE cloud

What would be proposed solution if customer wants to access ESXi management console using HTTPS, through Zscaler cloud. Does IT team need to authentication before accessing the server? How would request flow?

ZIA - Forwarding

7 answers

265 views

zywong

(Partner)

2 years ago

I presume the ESXi management console is sitting in private network, if this is the case this will be more of a ZPA proposal. 2 route can be taken:

Accessing through ZCC with some device posturing criteria

Tap on browser access feature probably with isolation to prevent any form of exporting the VM host

Pertaining to authentication, both route have their own authentication to complete (Identity of the user accessing / reaching to the ESXi page) and of cause the authentication towards the ESXi console for management of VMs

Generally, the flow of traffic will be:

User --> Zscaler Public Service Edge (ZPA) --> Hosted App Connector --> ESXi Server

Hope this helps to clarify.

2 likes

Geetanjali.geetanjali

(Partner)

2 years ago

But it would require app connector at every location where ESXi is hosted, correct? How would routing take place in internal DNS for private IP?

zywong

(Partner)

2 years ago

I not sure for yourself how many sites do have ESXi infrastructure if there are multiple physical sites would recommend to deploy the app connectors to all sites. But definitely its not 1 app connector to 1 apps, a single app connector can be used to serve multiple applications. But that being said, if your sites are interconnected you can deploy your app connector in 1 of the site and it can also connect to the rest of the ESXi infra (wont recommend but if resource constraint is there you can opt for this but do test it out if it is not too lag or etc.)

As for DNS, it will be tapping on your internal DNS servers to perform resolution. if you happen to recall on 1 of the steps for app connectors setup it will ask you to input the DNS server it will be used to resolve all FQDNs within your infra.

Routing will starts from your app connectors and resolution happens as an when needed and the app connector will reach out to the app the user request to access to.

zywong

Generally i wont recommend to use it with browser access because although the ESXi is hidden behind ZPA Cloud but it is used for hypervisor management as well as your virtual machines which also makes it critical. (Partner) asked a question.

How can browser access allow for 3rd party to access internal web site?

Hi,

I'm trying to make use of ZPA user portal for contractor to access our local resources through unmanaged device. It is fine to create user portal, withc public FQDN and CNAME.

However, there's problem on the portal link to access the local resources, with local domain, says .local. It's fine to access with ZCC. But, it can't on unmanaged device through browser local. Ramesh Mani

You have to record the CNAME entry in your public DNS to make it available over internet

Cname details will shown in the application segment itself. And the same has to be registered in DNS repository.

Hello @Mahesh Banka​ ,  You can review the below TS steps for further investigation

You will need to re-confirm if the whitelist is done properly as per the guide

https://config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa

, as usually this type of problems are due to some blocking or DNS resolution issue

Test connectivity to the upstream ZPA Public Service Edge by querying the DNS address

co2br.prod.zpath.net

from the server that is running the App Connector software.

[admin@localhost ~]$ dig +short

co2br.prod.zpath.net

13.60.119.37

42.68.244.163

Verify the TLS connection with the command below. A successful TLS connection results in a certificate subject string returned from the ZPA Public Service Edge.

openssl s_client -servername

mockcompany.com.server1.net

-connect 13.60.119.37:443 2>&1 | grep subject

Steps with required output is available on the

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/troubleshooting-app-connectors#cloudconnect

If you still face the issue, please share us the output and observation for the above commands.

BR

Jainil_G

10/12--> I have installed the ZCC on my windows 10 home private device. Exactly the same issue and behavior, so it is not definetly something related to the company device posture. What do we have then in common to verify? ZIA ? pac files? what else?

Hi, starting monday the 2nd of december we are experiencing a strange issue. We have 1200 users, more or less 3-400 connecting every with zpa from home. The strange thing is changing from wifi home to hotspot works for almost the user, sometimes user need to try 3 or 4 different mobile hotstpot before it is working. craig.plevinsky

likes this.

joemozdy

(Customer)

2 years ago

These 300-400 users, are they on wifi or wired connections? And are they mainly on Windows 11?

I ran into something similar sounding that was the result of some interactions with Windows Defender Firewall and some updates/changes the desktop support team made. Windows Defender Firewall has three profiles, Domain profile, Private profile, and Public profile. I found that in Windows 11, any wifi connection at all defaults to the Public profile, while any wired connection defaults to the Private profile. On the Public profile, some carrier grade NAT traffic is blocked that Zscaler uses for internal health checking and ZPA (

https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/zscaler-client-connector-processes-allowlist

). I followed that document when I ran into the issue, but wasn't able to find drop entries for the 100.64 addresses. That doesn't mean you shouldn't look, because there may be other underlying issues, just that I didn't find them.

A workaround/solution that I found was to have the user mark whatever network they were on as a private network instead of it being a public one. Another way to test this is to have the user use a wired connection, even if temporarily. This same behavior happens in Windows 10 as well, it's just that Windows 10 does not default all wifi connections as public networks and asks you when you first connect. Most people, or at least I do, would say that that their home wifi network is a personal network and not a public one, so I would expect to see that issue less on Windows 10 than 11. That's why I also suspect that some of your users have to try multiple wifi networks, because the ones that didn't work were marked public. Hope that helps!

## Can we use single App Connector for Different Application on different Subnets?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000Af3pBKCQY/can-we-use-single-app-connector-for-different-application-on-different-subnets
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-12-09T13:25:26.000Z

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

haider_mr

(Partner) asked a question.

December 9, 2024 at 5:30 AM

Can we use single App Connector for Different Application on different Subnets?

Hello!

I want to know whether we can use the same App connector for the multiple application residing in different Subnet?

OR we need to use different app connector for all the application residing on different subnets?

Also it is necessary to place app connector in the same subnet where the application is resided?

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

3 answers

479 views

Jainil_G

(Employee)

2 years ago

Hello @Haider Rangwala​  Below are best practices, and recommendation for the App connector deployment

Install the App Connectors on an internal network segment adjacent to the applications they are to provide connectivity to.

The App Connector should be configured to contact an internal DNS server capable of resolving hosts or internal servers for all the applications that need to be supported, as well as for hosts on the internet.

The App Connectors should have unrestricted access to the applications, with no protocol or port limitations or restrictions, including ICMP access.

The same App connector can be used for the multiple application residing in different Subnet, if AppC has proper network-level connectivity/routing with the application.

A brief information is available in the

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-connectors

BR

Jainil_G

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000Af4qhGCQQ/how-many-additional-vm-servers-are-required-for-fully-deploying-zia-zpa-zdx-on-client-environment-with-all-the-modules-enabled

How many additional VM servers are required for fully deploying ZIA, ZPA, ZDX on client environment with all the modules enabled?

Jainil_G

(Employee)

Hello @Rohin Ambati​ If you are referring to the App connector deployment, then you can review the below Prerequisites, which consists of requirement of ZPA, and ZDX.

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/connector-deployment-prerequisites

joemozdy

(Customer)

2 years ago

It's really going to depend on the structure of the network  you are putting them all on and your throughput. The app connectors should be deployed in pairs for redundancy and in an n+1 format as a best practice, and can handle 500mb/s of  traffic. Your networking team should be able to at least give you some sort of estimates about the amount of traffic in and out to help you figure out how many app connectors you have. The other driving factor is the structure of your network. If you have multiple network segments that don't/can't talk to each other, then you may need separate app connectors to put specifically in those network segments. If you have less network segments like that, then you could need fewer app connectors. Another factor is your what level of licensing you purchase. Different tiers can have a different amount of app connectors, check with  your TAM or sales rep about that part. Also dependent on your licensing (and your SIEM) is how many NSS and LSS servers you need. You may need at least one of each for ZIA and ZPA logs, more depending on the amount of logs you choose to send to your SIEM. Depending on the level of licensing you purchase and your SIEM, you may be able to set up a cloud to cloud log transmission as well.

I'd say your absolute minimum is going to be 8 servers, plus 2 optional ones for NSS and LSS. 2 servers as a pair to cover everything but network file shares, 2 servers as a pair handling only file shares, then 4 more servers doing the same thing at your disaster recovery site. But use that as a starting point, as it all depends on your specific needs.

In that case, you might need to install the Index Tool  in a VM which will allow you to create templates that can be applied in your Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries and engines that you would configure afterwards.

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-index-tool

You can also deploy that Index tool in an AWS EC2 instance, on an Azure VM.

## Show IP mapping of client public and private IP and server public and private IP in logs

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000ROKRd0AP/show-ip-mapping-of-client-public-and-private-ip-and-server-public-and-private-ip-in-logs
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-02-09T16:14:36.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Logging

rascs001

(Customer) asked a question.

January 23, 2025 at 4:25 AM

Show IP mapping of client public and private IP and server public and private IP in logs

From a client, when a server is pinged by FQDN, the client does not see the real IP address of the server. Some 100.x.x.x IP or such is seen. When client with a private iP of, say, 192.168.5.5 and public IP of, say, 3.4.5.6 access - using client connector - a server whose private IP is, say, 10.21.21.10, it is very hard for us to do any forensics on the server side because all the logs on the server shows the IP of app connector.

When we go to ZScaler, there isn't enough information to definitively tell that client with private IP of 192.168.5.5 and public IP of 3.4.5.6 connected to 10.21.21.10. The app connector must know all of this information.

Can you make logs available that will tell the public and private IP of a client and the public and private IP of the server it is connecting to and when?

If we had a situation where a client was doing nefarious activities, we want to correlate logs. We want such logs to flow into our SIEM product to generate alerts. Right now, we are running blind. We did a penetration test and attempted to follow logs from different systems and ZPA appears to be the bottleneck in tracing down activities of a pen tester. All logs on servers just point to the app connector and after that it becomes so hard to find which client was making responsible for making the request.

When we ping a server, can you just not show the IP of the server's FQDN instead of a fake IP?

ZPA - Logging

2 answers

746 views

avshch

likes this.

joemozdy

(Customer)

a year ago

You would be able to get this information right from the ZPA logs, either right in the ZPA console under the Analytics tab then select Diagnostics, or from those same logs forwarded to your you SEIM. The System Public IP address is a query-able field under the User section for the Diagnostic logs, but you would also be able to work backwards from knowing the application/server and ports that were connected to. You would also be able to search on the IP address of the app connector used along with the port from the app connector to the application/server connected to. There is a decent amount of information that is readily available that solves these issues you are facing. I'd talk with your internal team that handles ZPA to make sure that either log forwarding to your SEIM is being done appropriately with the needed fields, or getting access directly to the ZPA administrative console for the logs if appropriate. Also make sure that you know what the fields you need are.

Here is the link to the Zscaler help page on the Log Streaming Service, which also goes into detail about what logs have what fields, and what those fields describe:

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/log-streaming-service

And for your last question, no, you can't see the IP address of the server's FQDN instead of a synthetic IP address because it's not a direct conversation between you and the destination. You are sending the ping request to the app connectors via FQDN, then the app connectors execute that and give you back the results.

If you need the internal IP address of a destination application/server, you could ping from a jump box or other internal resource. The server's ip and port number being used are also part of the ZPA logs and are searchable under the Server IP:Port & Protocol field, along with the FQDN of the destination application/server.

The default for the synthetic range is 100.64.0.0/16,  but it can be adjusted to be anything from 100.64.0.0/16 to 100.127.0.0/16 in the Client Connector configuration if you need it to be something different for whatever reason.

rascs001

(Customer)

a year ago

Thank you, @Joe Mozdy​ , for your comments. Since  ZScaler cloud is brokering the connections between the client and the server, I was curious to see if ZScaler had the technology to respond to ping with the server's IP instead of the synthetic IP.

Based on your comments, it sounds like we might have to stream the logs to our SIEM where we can query information that is most suitable for our workflows. I appreciate you taking the time to respond with details.

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000ROdif0AD/show-urls-a-user-is-accessing-through-zpa
- Type: Q&A

rascs001

(Customer) asked a question.

January 23, 2025 at 4:15 AM

Show URLs a user is accessing through ZPA

We had a use case where a server CPU spiked. The server could only tell me that HTTP requests were coming from ZPA app connectors. So, I went to ZPA app connector to find out who was sending massive amount of requests and I couldn't find that. We asked support and they asked us to put a feature reqeust in.

Can you please expand your logging to show HTTP/HTTPS requests each client is making?

Client connector must know what resources each client is attempt to access, using which the app connector creates a microtunnel with the right server. It'd be great if you can log that and allow customers to download the log to debug issues. Such logging can be used for forensics as well in the case that a client is compromised and is sending malicious HTTP requests.

ZPA - Logging

5 answers

489 views

joemozdy

(Customer)

a year ago

Out of curiosity, why didn't you look in the ZPA console? I can think of multiple dashboard cards, as well as information under the Analytics tab such as Diagnostics or even Live Logs could have given you some of the information you seem to be looking for. If you know the destination, you can easily search for traffic on port 443 for your application in the logs.

The server CPU that spiked, was that an app connector? Or was someone connected to that server through ZPA, like trying to connect to a web console that is running on the target server? If your target server is the one making HTTP/HTTPS requests out and doesn't have it's traffic routed through Zscaler itself, I don't think the app connectors will be able to give you much information. You would have to check either server or firewall logs out for that sort of communication.

For example, Joe (a remote user at home) was hitting

Another user Bob (working out of a hotel) was hitting the same URL.

We wanted to know whether it was Bob hitting that URL a bunch of times or was it Joe. We also wanted to know which URLs Bob was hitting. From Diagnostics we could tell that Joe and Bob were both connected to an app connector and accessing an application but we couldn't find a way to tell what URLs they were hitting.

joemozdy

(Customer)

a year ago

So that information about them working their way down the domain tree, that's not information I would look for within ZPA. In your situation, I would look within the application logs, maybe on the server itself. I'd hope that your application is logging users and some level of activity. If this is a browser based application, you could also look at the browser based history to see exactly what pages were looked at, in addition to interviewing the users if need be. ZPA Diagnostics will tell you who connects to what through where but because of the microtunnel the activities aren't visible. That's not what it's designed to do, based on the name itself.

If your goal is being able to see those HTTP/HTTPS transactions because of different capabilities with applications or log gathering, in this situation you can also set up a forwarding policy to inspect traffic of certain ZPA application segments with ZIA,

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-forwarding-policy#source-ip-anchoring

. You do need a license for this though. If you application has its own internal logs, I'd go that route first.

How to force off trusted user to connect private ZPA PSE and never to connect to public ZPA

what is that best option we can force off trusted network user to connect to private PSE and never connect to public ZPA other then the proximity option.

ZPA - Forwarding

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Siraj Rana​  The ZPA redirection policy can be configured to prefer ZPA Private Service Edges over ZPA Public Service Edges.

The ZPA Private Service Edge Selection Method can be configured with 'Always,' which will redirect users only to the target ZPA Private Service Edges, and no fallback to ZPA Public Service Edges will be provided.

Ref:

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-redirection-policy

BR

## ZPA SCIM Attribute

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000RiOdW0AV/zpa-scim-attribute
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-02-10T07:13:26.000Z

ZPA - Authentication

amandeep009

(Customer) asked a question.

January 28, 2025 at 6:45 PM

ZPA SCIM Attribute

Hi,

I wanted to understand why Group attribute is not required in Azure AD when we are integrating Azure AD with Zscaler.

In below guide also Zscaler team only suggested to use Group attribute in ZPA but not in ZIA.

Zscaler and Azure Identity Deployment Guide | Zscaler

Can anyone please help me to understand the logic behind this??

Thanks

Amandeep

ZPA - Authentication

1 answer

315 views

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Amandeep Dhiman​ , The group attribute is one of the attributes that can help with policy configuration in ZIA and ZPA. However, it is not mandatory to use the group attribute for ZIA/ZPA, as you can configure policies using other user attributes as well.

One possible reason for highlighting it in the deployment guide for ZPA is related to entitlements: for ZIA, entitlements appear grayed out i.e. applicable for all users/group, and for ZPA, depending on the licenses you have and the initial testing phase, you might have the option to enable it for specific groups, conduct tests, and then proceed with a broader rollout.

Additionally, SAML/SCIM attributes such as username, group or department will be used for least privilege access policy restriction, which would be more important for the Internal/Private Applications compare to Internet services

BR
