## App connector deploy in DR should be in same app coonector group of main DC or separate

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000SBMoK0AX/app-connector-deploy-in-dr-should-be-in-same-app-coonector-group-of-main-dc-or-separate
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-02-13T09:25:16.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

sirajrana

(Partner) asked a question.

February 5, 2025 at 8:23 AM

App connector deploy in DR should be in same app coonector group of main DC or separate

Hi ,

We have client who has one app coonector in DC and wants another app coonector in DR site.So what should be the best practise to deplay this app coonector?

Can this app coonector in two diffrent location in same city can be group in same appcoongroup or has to deploy in diffrent appgroup ? Can both this ap coonector in diffrention laction work in cluster ?

Or Customer should have 2 xAPpcoon in one DC in cluster and one in DR ?

Or customer can have 1xApp in DC and 1X DR to work in cluster in same appConnector group ?

ZPA - Forwarding

3 answers

319 views

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

Let's start to first understand the

App Connector Deployment Best Practices

1. Deploy 2x App Connectors per Site for Redundancy:

It is a best practice to deploy at least two App Connectors per site (Primary DC and DR site) for redundancy purposes. This ensures high availability (HA) in case one App Connector fails.

ZPA ACs operate in an active/active architecture, reducing dependency on a single connector.

2. Location-Based Segmentation of Connectors:

Deploy separate App Connector Groups based on physical locations (i.e., DC and DR, if they are in different physical sites).

Even if the primary DC and the DR site are located in the same city, they should ideally have different App Connector Groups to ensure proper load balancing, traffic routing, and easier failover management between DC and DR.

Answers to your Questions

A1. Can App Connectors in Two Different Locations (Same City) Be Grouped in the Same App Connector Group?

Recommendation: No, it’s not recommended. (Explained above)

A2. Can Both App Connectors in Different Locations Work in a Cluster?

App Connectors do not form clusters across different physical locations.

App Connector failover and traffic distribution occur within the same App Connector Group, so placing connectors from different sites in the same group could lead to traffic being routed to a distant DR site unnecessarily, impacting performance.

A3. Should the Customer Have 2x App Connectors in One DC and 1x in DR Site?

This approach is not ideal because redundancy within the DR site would be missing.

If the DR App Connector fails, there would be no alternative, causing a disruption for the DR site applications.

A4. Can the Customer Have 1x App Connector in DC and 1x in DR in the Same App Connector Group?

While technically possible, this is NOT recommended for reasons of performance and failover efficiency:

Traffic intended for the primary DC could get routed to the DR App Connector unnecessarily (and vice versa), leading to higher latency.

If there is a failure in one App Connector, traffic cannot effectively failover within the same site—it would unnecessarily failover to the other site.

Note : If cost or resources are a concern, the customer could deploy:

1x App Connector in DC for critical production apps.

2x App Connectors in the DR site for resilience during failover.

However,

this approach is not recommended

since it reduces production-site redundancy and is less reliable than deploying 2x App Connectors in both locations.

Final Recommendations

Primary DC: At least 2x App Connectors, configured in the DC App Connector Group.

DR Site: At least 2x App Connectors, configured in the DR App Connector Group

1 like

Gianluca.bastia

(Partner)

a year ago

Is the DR Site an active standby, or a replica of the VMs that get spun up when a DR event happens?

Either way, the DR app connectors should be in their own group. And replication of App Connectors is NOT recommended.

I have a customer who has DR app connectors, and they are not linked to any Server Group. Once a DR situation happens, the DR app connector group would be linked to the server group and would start participating in the traffic routing.

It had to be done in this scenario because the DR site is an exact replica (including IPs) and therefore production traffic was being sent to DR resources.

sirajrana

(Partner)

a year ago

It has to be active standby

APP Connector OVA file having error while installtion

Hi team,

When using ovf package to deploy app connector I am getting below error

Cause:

a specific parameter was not correct

the checksum from the provided manifest file do not match the content of files

ZPA - Admin Portal

sirajrana

(Partner)

a year ago

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

Hi @Siraj Rana​

This usually is an error thrown when the ova file which was tried in the deployment is corrupt.

The OVA image must be downloaded again from

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/connector-deployment-guide-vmware-platforms#VM_VCENTER

This can be verified by checking the hash value of the contents of downloaded file and comparing with the original.

For this, extract the downloaded ova file in a folder. You will get 3 files from the OVA:

*.mf

*.ovf

*.vmdk

Using command prompt/terminal, check the SHA1 hash value of the vmdk file. Command is:

certutil -hashfile filename.vmdk SHA1 (windows)

sha1sum filename.vmdk (linux)

Compare this SHA1 hash value with the one present in *.mf file. This file can be opened with notepad/other text editor.

The SHA1 hash value of the downloaded files must match with the ones in "mf" file. If there is a mismatch, one would see the error as mentioned at the top while image deployment.

adeeshar

(Partner) asked a question.

February 17, 2025 at 3:41 PM

Zscaler ZIA and ZPA IdP migration

Hey Guys,

We are planning to migrate existing Google authentication IdP to Azure AD. Currently we haven't deployed SCIM Provisioning. However we want to deploy SCIM provisioning with new Azure IdP. I am expecting a proper guidance on how to migrate IdP successfully.

Thank you

ZIA - Authentication

4 answers

530 views

joemozdy

(Customer)

a year ago

Here is the help document about moving to a new idp;

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/migrating-new-saml-idp

It says to make sure that for SCIM provisioning, the username fields need to be the same between the new and old idps, along with all the same information present in both. When you go to add the new idp, there is a wizard to handle the migration. I'd get with your TAM to make sure you have all the resources lined up, but it does seem like the process is relatively straight forward once you get over the hill of making sure the two idps are synced up.

adeeshar

(Partner)

a year ago

Hey Joemozdy,

Thank you for your response. But I got a doubt. Currently we are not using SCIM provisioning with Google IdP. But we are planning to use it with Azure IdP. In that case what are the attributes we need to consider?

joemozdy

(Customer)

a year ago

That's really going to come down to what fields you find are important, that you want to make use of. Certainly things like userid, but I would recommend things like title and department at least. Really anything that can be used to describe a user or group of users. Like if you have a field that identifies external contractors, or one that might identify VIP users.

I don't think the fact that you aren't using SCIM for your Google idp matters too much in this situation, just that the username attribute is the same between the Google idp and Azure idp. Azure uses the email address as the username attribute, and I would be surprised if Google worked differently in that manner.

Gianluca.bastia

(Partner)

a year ago

From a ZIA perspective, the only attribute you can use in policy is the "Department". ZPA allows for much more granularity and can leverage custom attributes that you see fit.

The fact that you are currently not using SCIM, makes me think you are not utilizing any special attributes, therefore I would focus on migrating IdP first, and then ones that process is complete, review the attributes and pro/cons of adding if needed.

## Bypass/Forwarding Options/Policies on Zscaler

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000T0D5N0AV/bypassforwarding-optionspolicies-on-zscaler
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-03-01T07:39:31.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

PaulZir

(Customer) asked a question.

February 19, 2025 at 3:23 PM

Bypass/Forwarding Options/Policies on Zscaler

In our enviroment, ZPA (Packet Filter Based Mode) runs on our clients in order to connect to the global corporate network. To clarify it, we do not manage ourselves the Zscaler.

So, I am not familiar with Zscaler Mgmt GUI. It is managed by other independent Team.

But I would like to ask which possibilities could offer Zscaler in our use case.

From our side we want to reach some destinations/servers which are located in isolated enviroment within the global corporate network, not over Zscaler but over other VPN Solution.

Let's say a traditional VPN Remote Access Solution which builds a virtual adapter on the client and assigns an IP from the VPN IP Pool.

So, we are talking about Split-Tunneling case where probably the intended traffic to the desired server Y.Y.Y.Y has to be bypassed on Zscaler so that it can be forwarded to the other VPN remote access client.

I am aware that generally it is possible to bypass traffic to specific Server from Zscaler tunnel, but we do not want to have a global impact to all clients/users.

It's should be more user-based.

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-bypass-settings

Based on the documentation above the key elements are: Client Forwarding Policies, application segment etc.

As I known, for User Identification/Auth Zscaler works with Azure Entra-ID.

Is it possible to build a bypass policy/policies for a single user or for a group of users, so that they could reach the server Y.Y.Y.Y over an other way and not via Zscaler?

It should be like this:

Source: User-ID or Group of User => Destination: Y.Y.Y.Y  Action: Bypass

It would be ideal if the dest_port/service could be also filtered in the above theoretical policy.

Does it sound possible impelementation on Zscaler? Does anyone have any similar experience?

Thank you in advance.

ZPA - Forwarding

3 answers

1.53K views

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Pavlos Ziridis​ , If I understand your requirement correctly, your current setup is as follows:

User (ZCC) -> Zscaler -> Global Corporate Network via ZPA (to access the resources).

Your requirement, however, is to enable access to an isolated network via VPN, and you want this setup to be applied on a per-user basis:

User (VPN Solution) -> Direct Internet -> VPN Concentrator -> Global Corporate Network (Isolated).

In this scenario, you can create a new App Profile for the required users and add the VPN Gateway IP for them. This configuration will bypass all VPN gateway traffic for those users (Isolated - Global Corporate Network), while normal ZPA traffic will continue to function as expected through Zscaler (Global Corporate Network).

BR

Jainil_G

PaulZir

(Customer)

a year ago

Hello @Jainil Gajjar​ ,

thank you very much for your response.

The user's VPN Client will reach over Zscaler/Global Network our VPN GW (the one what you called Concetrator) in order to build a separate SSLVPN Tunnel.

(The VPN GW, has a corporate private address, no Internet is involved).

And then the user should get remote access to desired destinations in the isolated enviroment. So, this VPN Solution will run on top of Zscaler.

Therefore bypass is needed on Zscaler towards the intended destinations, otherwise ZCC (which works on Packet Filter Based Mode, Windows Filter driver) will grab

the traffic to desired destinations before it reaches the virtual Adapter of the VPN solution.

It is more like this:

User (VPN Client) => Zscaler/Global Corporate Network => VPN GW

Tunnel is established and then: User Client => desired destinations/isolated enviroment (bypassed on Zscaler)

Hope it is clear now.

Would be in this scenario also your recommendation with App Profile for specific users suitable?

Is it possible from your side to provide us some screenshots to see how this could be done on Zscaler?

Thank you and BR,

Pavlos

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Pavlos Ziridis​  Thank you for the detailed explanation. Based on my understanding, this seems to be a complex setup, and there is a likelihood of interoperability issues arising. In my opinion, this setup adds unnecessary complexity because ZPA is designed for direct application access without requiring a VPN.

If a VPN is mandatory, users would need to first connect to ZPA and then establish a VPN session to access the isolated network (Internal Access VPN as no Internet for Isolated). This could result in tunnel conflicts, increased latency, and potential connectivity issues.

For the bypass requirement, we could explore bypassing traffic to the isolated IP, for example, 10.1.1.1, via VPN from Zscaler by using the Client Forwarding Policy (

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-client-forwarding-policies

) with the "Bypass ZPA" option. Additionally, we could restrict access to specific users, groups, or departments via SAML/SCIM attributes. However, I have serious doubts about whether this would work as intended, and even if it does, the connectivity challenges might persist. This would require advanced discussions and thorough testing before drawing any conclusions.

BR

Jainil_G

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Punit Mandelia​ It is strongly recommended to update the host operating system (OS) and software packages before using the App Connector in production. This helps mitigate major security vulnerabilities that have been discovered in Linux. Performing updates at least on a monthly basis is advised.

Essentially, there are three types of updates that need attention:

App Connector Version Upgrade: This is performed automatically based on the scheduled configuration for the App Connector upgrade.

Host OS and Software Update: This needs to be performed manually following the guide:

Updating App Connector Host OS and Software Packages

Manager Version Update: This also requires manual intervention, as outlined in the guide:

Understanding Manager Software

The Manager software is included as part of upgrades to the App Connector, ZPA Private Service Edge, or Private Cloud Controller host operating system (OS).

BR

Jainil_G

## DNS Search Domains Appended to FQDN

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000VIJfP0AX/dns-search-domains-appended-to-fqdn
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-04-04T15:20:58.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Admin Portal

ozanogur

(Partner) asked a question.

April 1, 2025 at 10:34 AM

DNS Search Domains Appended to FQDN

Dear Community,

we have several search domains in our ZPA Tenant configured, and as far as I read in the documentation from Zscaler these search domains should be appended to the shortnames in the client side. For example if user do the following;

shortname: server1

search domains in ZPA portal: xyz.com, abc.com

The results should be something like this : server1. xyz.com and server1.abc.com

But what I see in the client connector logs, that when the application I have tries to connect FQDN directly (e.g. server1. xyz.com ), I am still seeing that the it tries to add other domain to the FQDN and gives me something like this: server1. xyz.com.abc.com

Does anyone have any ideas

ZPA - Admin Portal

3 answers

477 views

punit.mandelia

(Customer)

a year ago

For this you need to define those servers with respective FQDN's in the application segment

ozanogur

(Partner)

a year ago

The application segment already defined with the fqdn.

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Ozan Ogur​ The way the search domain works is as follows: when any application is accessed using its short name, the DNS search suffixes configured on the machine are appended to the hostname/short name to form a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN). For example, given the configuration below:

Short name: server1

Search domains in the ZPA portal:

xyz.com

abc.com

If someone accesses the application as server1, the machine will append

xyz.com

to create

server1.xyz.com

. However, if you/application directly access

server1.xyz.com

, the search domain suffix might still be appended, resulting in something like

server1.xyz.com.xyz.com

i.e non-existing domain.

You can easily check this functionality from your machine by performing an

nslookup server1

from the command prompt. When a valid FQDN matches the app segments, ZCC returns a synthetic IP address to facilitate the transaction. If no match is found, it returns an NXDOMAIN error.

BR

Jainil_G

Jainil_G

Hello @sudheerpaul elamala​ , Client forwarding policy is not directly visible in the ZPA diagnostic logs. The general logic is that if the traffic is bypassed via CFP, it won’t appear in the ZPA diagnostic logs. However, traffic passing through ZPA will already be visible in the diagnostic logs. As a result, CFP is not directly shown in the logs. If there are multiple policies, you need to evaluate them.

BR

Jainil_G

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

One way to find out traffic that is bypassed by the CFP by design is to look into the ZCC Logs.

It will still not give you visibility into the matched CFP,  but you can find what traffic was bypassed using the keywork "always bypass" or "bypass cache"

Another thing that you can enable to see what traffic is sent not via ZCC but over plain internet is by enabling

Flow Logging

and it will

report traffic flows to ZIA

from the following flows:

VPN:

VPN connection (outer tunnel toward VPN server)

VPN tunnel:

Inner tunnel traffic (actual traffic flows within the VPN tunnel)

Direct:

Direct internet traffic

Intranet:

RFC 1918, IPv6 Intranet

Loopback:

Loopback IPv4 and IPv6

Block traffic:

T2 fallback option, drop IPv6 configuration, block due to strict enforcement mode, block due to disaster recovery configuration

You must

enable

Install WFP Driver

to use this feature.

## ZPA SE: Session closed by Service Edge

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000W7WYq0AN/zpa-se-session-closed-by-service-edge
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-04-17T07:06:33.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Logging

JM

(Partner) asked a question.

April 16, 2025 at 12:56 AM

ZPA SE: Session closed by Service Edge

Based on the diagnostics, the Action is Allow, but in status code SE: Session closed by Service Edge.

What does it mean?

Also the website is inaccessible by that time but it is now working out of nowhere.

Can anyone explain?

It is a website. The TCP Keep alive in the app segment is already enabled.

ZPA - Logging

2 answers

421 views

Top Rated Answers

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

It's a standard/graceful closure.

You shouldn't consider it as a problem/error.

It is just an message indicating that ZPA Service Edge has received termination on the mtunnel from both the client side and app connector side, so the mtunnel is not needed anymore and ZPA Service Edge would also terminate it. There is no action required for this message.

I'm experiencing packet loss to the default gateway when connected to Wi-Fi while using Zscaler ZIA+ZPA. The issue does

not

occur when using a wired connection. Disabling the Zscaler Client Connector resolves the problem on Wi-Fi.

Has anyone encountered that?

manuel

Looks like the classic MTU issue for me.

Try to figure out the correct MTU size of your connection WITHOUT Zscaler Client active and then modify setting in Fwd Profile accordingly. You can also try directly setting the MTU to 1370 or enable MTU Path Discovery if you did not so yet. Also check the forum here and search for "MTU". You will find a whole bunch of some aged comments about issues with MTU.

BR

Manuel

Hello,

hm, there should be no issue downloading the rpm packages . Which URL did you use? The official RH9 packages can be found here:

MikeRuiz

a year ago

RPM install is NOT supported on CentOS9.  RPM based install is ONLY supported on RedHat 8 or RedHat 9 as the base OS.  For use on any other linux distributions you should use the app connector docker container.

Please note the RPM for RHEL8 and RHEL9 are different repositories as well.

ad01 :389 UDP/TCP and TCP 135/445 and 55925 TCP are in use mostly

1 like

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

a year ago

TCP/88: Kerberos

TCP/464: Kerberos Password Change

TCP/389: LDAP

TCP/3268: Global Catalog

TCP/3269: Global Catalog SSL (Optional)

TCP/135: MSRPC

TCP/139: Common Internet File Service (CIFS)

TCP/445: CIFS

UDP/88: Kerberos

UDP/464: Kerberos Password Change

UDP/389: LDAP

UDP/636: LDAPS (Optional)

UDP/138: NetBT datagram (File Server)

UDP/123: NTP Service

Note that it's historically been wise to incldue both TCP and UDP for these as Microsoft has often switched between TCP and UDP without documentation reflecting it.

Also have a wildcard for the root of your forest so that all the relevant SRV records can easily be resolved.  That wildcard doesn't necessarily need all these ports open if you are covering the relevant servers via FQDNs.  The wildcard only needs a single port at a minimum, even 1-1.

alissonvieira

(Partner) asked a question.

July 3, 2025 at 3:31 PM

Unexpected pop-up: "Application access is blocked by private access policy"

We are experiencing an issue where a pop-up message is displayed with the following text:

"Application access is blocked by private access policy"

I understand that this message indicates that some traffic is being blocked by the private access policy. However, my policy is configured as follows:

Block all access > Pop-Up Message to User > Disable

In the ZCC panel, I also checked under

Client Connector Notification

, and all fields are set to

Disable

I would like to confirm if there is any other point I may have forgotten to disable. My client requests that this pop-up

not be displayed

, but I am having trouble preventing it from appearing.

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

1 answer

1.51K views

Eric N.

likes this.

Jainil_G

(Employee)

a year ago

Hello @Alisson Vieira​ The feature you are referring to—'Block all access > Pop-Up Message to User > Disable'—is available starting from ZCC version 4.7, which is currently under limited availability. I am not sure if your users have that version. If not, this feature will not work.

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/release-upgrade-summary-2025?applicable_category=private.zscaler.com&deployment_date=2025-05-19&id=1529417

Regarding the notification: 'Notification: Application Access is blocked by Private Access Policy.' By default, users are expected to see block notifications when access is denied. However, you can disable all Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) notifications by navigating to More > Settings and disabling 'Show all notifications' in the Zscaler Client Connector. This will completely turn off all notifications.

If you have made this change and the issue persists, you can try completely exiting ZCC, restarting it, or rebooting the system once.

BR

Jainil_G

## Kerberos pre-authentication failed w/ ZPA

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000aqJef0AE/kerberos-preauthentication-failed-w-zpa
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-11-04T23:53:26.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

(Partner) asked a question.

Kerberos pre-authentication failed w/ ZPA

In a recent ZPA deployment I have encountered an issue whereby Kerberos authentication requests via ZPA App Connector are getting the following error from Domain Controller. Client's are able to authenticate without issue with ZPA is not in play.

4771(F): Kerberos pre-authentication failed.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4771#security-monitoring-recommendations.

Examining the PCAP from the AC we can see this Kerberos error being reflected with the..

KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED

KRB5KDC_ERR_PADATA_TYPE_NOSUPP

... errors (see below).

All Domain Controller App Segments have been configured directly in line with Mark Ryan' brilliant articles on this subject (

here

).

Has anyone encounter any similar issues when doing Kerberos auth through ZPA AC's?

ZPA - Forwarding

1 answer

502 views

Dirk_Monge

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Evan Spal​

I advise  to confirm whether the authentication process is targeting the same server IP address in both working and non-working cases. A discrepancy here could indicate variations in server configurations, which need to be addressed.

Step 1: Validate the Server IP:

When the issue occurs on ZPA, you can verify the server IP address by navigating to ZPA Portal > Analytics > Diagnostics > User Activity.

Filter the activity logs by the appropriate username, server domain, and timeframe.

Check the Server IP listed in the last column and compare it against the working scenario.

If there is a mismatch, this discrepancy likely points to differences in server setup or configuration in the affected environment.

Step 2: Health-Check for IP Retransmissions:

Analyze the capture file (e.g., "

CaptureAdapter… .pcap

" from ZCC logs) and check for potential retransmissions to a relevant internal private IP address.

Retransmissions might indicate that the client has  cached the server IP and might try to reach it directly instead of using domain name/fqdn. If the IP of server is not added in ZPA, only FQDN based access would work.

Use Wireshark with the following filter to validate retransmissions: tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.analysis.retransmission

Step 3: Verify SRV Record Resolutions:

Compare working and non-working cases for any SRV resolution discrepancies.

SRV resolutions are critical for certain protocols, including Kerberos

Use Wireshark to troubleshoot SRV record queries with the following filter: dns.qry.type == 33

Identify any differences between the two cases to uncover potential misconfigurations on the DNS or server side.

Step 4: Server-Side Analysis:

Based on the provided screenshot, the ZPA functionality has been confirmed as operational, allowing for end-to-end communication.

Therefore, it is crucial to work closely with the server support team to determine why authentication requests are being rejected when traffic is routed through ZPA. The server logs will help identify whether any specific conditions or configurations are contributing to the failure.

Regards.

Hi Sunil,

This can be achieved via ZPA public API, if the developer use Postman appin their development, they can leverage Zscaler API integration, this will help them to add or remove FQDNs form the respective app segment, below is the article for Zscaler ZPA public API

Ronnie Meekers

(Partner)

a year ago

There are risks involved by giving this level of access directly to developers. for example, there is no RBAC available for the ZPA API.

It's also important to to validate the URLs being entered. you would want to avoid wildcard entries, etc...

Ideally, this type of setup is done through code repository/terraform integration where you have the option to perform peer review/approval before URLs are added.

Or alternatively, I'm assuming you're to PaaS FQDNs here, you integrate to the API call to ZPA as part of the pipeline that builds the PaaS services.

Abu Bakar

Greetings,

Thanks for your valuable insights @Ronnie Meekers​  and @Osho Dwivedi​ , connectivity issue was the half the story here, see I am trying to deploy the PSE using the docker method as per Zscaler KB article, as I follow through the documentation everthing was fine and up and running even my PSE was reflecting in my ZPA portal the issue was with command specific to port forwarding in the docker container, as I deployed the PSE the private IP which was reflecting over there was docker default bridge IP 172.17.0.0/16 and my docker host IP was 10.0.0.x series that's why there were no connectivity to my PSE from my Windows Host system, to overcome this situation I need to go through the drawing board and brush up my docker networking and then I realize that there is a way to rectify this docker networking issue as make my container use my host machine IP instead default docker bridge network, and tweak the command and redeployed my docker container and waited for the end result and finally my Windows host was able to access my PSE in the ZCC. It was a fun experience.

## A single server group vs two or more server groups

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000boSkB0AU/a-single-server-group-vs-two-or-more-server-groups
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-07-30T10:32:09.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Forwarding

jaicybersec

(Customer) asked a question.

July 25, 2025 at 12:13 AM

A single server group vs two or more server groups

For example, we have 4 app connectors to an app segment.

Scenario 1

we assign two app connectors to a server group and assign remaining two to another server group and add these two server groups to the app segment. Now the app segment contains two server groups. How ZPA will work in this condition when client machine or ZPA user wants to access the app segment.

Scenario 2

We assign all 4 app connectors to a single server group and assign the server group to the app segment. now the app segment has a single server group. How ZPA work in this condition when client machine or ZPA wants to access the app segment.

Which one is the best for active directory related app segments and why ?

Which one is the best for normal applications related app segment and why ?

Kindly help me on this.

ZPA - Forwarding

3 answers

343 views

Top Rated Answers

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

Let's break the scenarios down and answer your questions step by step:

Scenario 1: Two Server Groups with Two App Connectors Each

Setup: You distribute the 4 App Connectors evenly between two server groups (two App Connectors per server group) and assign these two server groups to the app segment.

How ZPA Works:

When a client machine (or ZPA user) attempts to access the app segment, ZPA's intelligent traffic routing will decide which server group to use via a load-balanced or policy-based decision.

Within the chosen server group, one of the two App Connectors will be selected to facilitate the connection to the app segment.

This setup is useful for redundancy and geographic distribution, as the server groups can be localized to specific regions or datacenters.

Scenario 2: Single Server Group with All Four App Connectors

Setup: You assign all 4 App Connectors to a single server group and assign that server group to the app segment.

How ZPA Works:

In this scenario, ZPA will utilize any of the 4 App Connectors in the server group to make the connection to the application.

This setup allows for all connections to be managed within one server group, consolidating management and potentially simplifying rule creation.

All connectors within the group provide redundancy and load balancing, but all App Connectors will be treated as part of the same logical entity.

Which Scenario is Best for Active Directory (AD)-Related App Segments?

Scenario 1 is generally preferred for AD-related app segments. Here’s why:

Redundancy and Isolation: Active Directory is a critical infrastructure component, and isolating its server groups by geography or functionality (e.g., primary and backup data centers) provides additional failover reliability.

Load Balancing and Localization: AD traffic can be latency-sensitive, especially for authentication requests like LDAP, Kerberos, etc. By dividing the App Connectors into two server groups, you can reduce latency by routing users to the geographically closest or most efficient group.

Flexibility: If any connector or server group fails, the other group can still serve the authentication requests, supporting high availability.

Which Scenario is Best for Normal Application-Related App Segments?

Scenario 2 is typically better for normal application-related app segments. Here’s why:

Simplified Management: Consolidating all App Connectors into a single server group simplifies server group management. This is sufficient for most normal applications where performance and redundancy requirements are not as critical as with AD.

Resource Pooling: By grouping all connectors together, the resource capacity of all App Connectors becomes available to serve the app segment. This is often more than enough to handle typical application traffic.

Reduced Complexity: For applications that are not latency-sensitive or do not require geographic separation, keeping everything in a single group reduces operational complexity.

JB

scenario 1:  app segment with 2 server groups (2 app connectors each)

setup:

app segment -> contains server group a (2 app connectors) + server group b (2 app connectors)

total: 4 app connectors, but logically separated

behavior:

when a user attempts to access the application, the zscaler cloud will select one of the server groups to establish the path based on health, load, location, etc.

zpa will only use one server group per connection, not both simultaneously.

if one server group becomes unavailable example app connectors go down the other server group is used as a failover - if healthy.

useful for resiliency, geographic redundancy, or split data center access.

scenario 2: all 4 app connectors in a single server group

setup:

app segment -> contains 1 server group with all 4 app connectors

behavior:

zscaler will load balance connections among all 4 app connectors.

all connectors are treated equally for availability and performance.

single logical unit, no redundancy across groups, but better connector level load distribution.

which is better for each use case?

for active directory-related app segments

best option: scenario 1 – two separate server groups

for normal business application segments

best option: scenario 2 – single server group with all app connectors

## ZPA  on/off trusted network

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000bxKwf0AE/zpa-onoff-trusted-network
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-07-28T16:42:36.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Deception

Diode

(Customer) asked a question.

July 28, 2025 at 11:36 AM

ZPA  on/off trusted network

Hi recently deployed ZPA for our users and all are good. All ZPA users are treated a off trusted network and no b/w issues yet. I have deployed 2 app connectors per site. What's the best way to tell ZCC if the users are in the office bypass ZPA and directly go to our on-pram app/service etc.. May be ping our local G/W and if yes treat as on trusted network ? We have windows and macs and users need to reboot the devices ? Also I have licences to 2 x PSE will this help ? Looking for some advise . Cheers

ZPA - Deception

6 answers

762 views

Top Rated Answers

JB

(Partner)

a year ago

your 2x PSE licenses can help

If users are in the office, instead of going to ZPA Public Service Edges over the internet, traffic can route to the on-prem PSE for lower latency.

This doesn’t bypass ZPA but improves performance and keeps traffic local to your environment.

Combine this with trusted network detection to decide when to bypass ZPA or when to route locally through the PSE.

To implement this:

Define Trusted Network in the ZCC Portal using:

DNS suffixes (e.g., internal domain like .corp.local)

Internal DNS resolvers (like internal AD/DNS IPs)

Gateway IPs (pinging local default gateway is a valid method, but you don’t need custom scripts – ZCC can check gateway IP)

Create ZPA Forwarding profile policy:

Set the profile to disable ZPA tunnel if the device is on a trusted network.

You can configure fallback options if the network is not trusted.

Difference between SIPA and ZPA

Hi,

Can someone please clarify — if we dont use SIPA and route traffic to internet-hosted applications via ZPA App Connector, will the traffic still egress with the App Connector's fixed public IP? I’m trying to understand whether SIPA is truly necessary in scenarios where ZPA is already deployed on the user system.

In our current setup, traffic flows from ZCC to ZPA, then through the App Connector to the destination internet server

if we dont use SIPA and route traffic to internet-hosted applications via ZPA App Connector, will the traffic still egress with the App Connector's fixed public IP?    -

Yes it will use APP connector public IP.

security controls in ZIA

SIPA will add up more security controls leverage from ZIA.

All Answers

JB

(Partner)

a year ago

no, zpa app connector is not designed to provide internet egress on behalf of users. if your traffic is destined for internet-hosted applications like

https://app.salesforce.com

and you try to route that traffic via zpa and the app connector without sipa, the traffic will not egress using the app connector’s fixed public ip.

zpa app connector default behavior:

zpa is designed to provide zero trust access to private/internal applications, not internet-based services.

when a user accesses a private app via zpa, the app connector makes an outbound connection to zscaler and establishes a reverse tunnel for application access. it does not act as a forward proxy to the internet.

even if the app connector has a fixed public ip, it won’t be used to forward internet-bound traffic like a proxy. zpa won’t direct traffic to public saas applications through the app connector unless sipa is used.

use case for sipa:

sipa allows zpa app connectors to also forward traffic to specific internet-hosted apps as a proxy, enabling internet-bound traffic to egress through controlled public ips (usually for ip whitelisting on saas platforms like salesforce etc.).

with sipa enabled, specific traffic (to allowed internet domains) is routed via zpa app connector and egresses via its fixed public ip, which can then be whitelisted at the saas provider.

Osho_Dwivedi

(Employee)

a year ago

What Ramesh mentioned is absolutely on point.

The idea to have SIPA is to publish the web application as private but still be able to enforce all the ZIA Policy Engines to the traffic, just for egressing out it uses the App Connector's public IP.

In order to test the first scenario, you can use

whatismyipaddress.com

or

ipchicken.com

published as a ZPA Application, and you'd see app connector's IP on the website as your egress IP. Although that traffic will never end up on ZIA.

With SIPA, the behaviour would be that your traffic will hit ZIA enforcing all the policy controls and break out via the APP Connector. This is achieved through a client forwarding policy.

Proper configuration for Source IP Anchoring in ZPA requires the following Client Forwarding Policies for domain-based and IP address-based applications:

For IP address-based applications, select the Only Forward Allowed Applications rule action for Source IP Anchoring segment groups.

For domain-based applications, configure the following rules:

Rule 1: Enable the Bypass ZPA rule action for both Segment Groups and Client Types > Client Connector.

Rule 2: Enable the Forward to ZPA rule action for both Segment Groups and Client Types > ZIA Service Edge.

As a rule of thumb, use FQDNs/domain based applications instead of IP based.

BlueSocks

(Partner)

4 months ago

Both SIPA and Classic ZPA whitelisting

use app connectors as exit points. ZPA was designed for private applications, but you can put public destinations in app segments. The main reason for this in production is because of some conditional access requirement like IP Whitelisting at the destination.

The main difference between the two is 1) minimalist licensing requirements 2) how traffic flows from client connector.

Classic ZPA Whitelisting.

Minimalist licensing: ZPA only.

Traffic flows from

client connector, to ZPA,

to app connector, to destination app.

Notice the bold text above, the traffic flows from laptop direclty to zpa. This is the key difference.

SIPA

Minimalist licensing is ZIA only with SIPA addon. The SIPA addon gets you a lightweight ZPA dashboard login, even though you didn't think you were buying ZPA, you get a zpa dashboard login so you can configure app connectors and app segments.

Traffic flows from

client connector, to ZIA,

to app connector, to destination app.

Notice here the traffic flow goes to ZIA first.

So now the question is why choose SIPA over Classic....  the main reason is simply to be able to inspect the traffic with all the built in ZIA tools.

That's what it boils down to.

This only needs to be opened on the firewall if you have 3rd party applications / connections communicating directly to our database and requiring access to the port number MariaDB is running on (not general users).

Optimus - Apache Tomcat Webserver

8080 – Do I need to open this for all users ?

This will need to be opened for any users wishing to run remote web based applications against the Optimus server. I believe you were talking to a colleague here about access to Optimus Webservices for your API’s. These connect to Apache Tomcat running on port 8080. You also have a reporting writing tool (Dataflex) that also runs through Apache Tomcat. The access will probably be for DBA’s and report writers rather than general Optimus users but you would need to check who requires access to the Tomcat webservice.

Optimus - Department RDC

8070 – Do I need to open this for all users ?

This will need to be opened for any user wishing to run the Optimus Department RDC application from within their local web browsers. I do not who or how many users you have running this application but this is not used by the general Optimus users running the Dash application.

Diode

(Customer)

a year ago

This is what I got form the app supplier

MariaDB Server -

uses port 3306

– Do these needs to all users or just for DBA’s ?

This is the port that MariaDB listens on for incoming connections

When the Optimus client(s) request access to one of the Optimus server side executables, this will open a

‘dynamic’

port number on the server for the connection. These will be the port numbers you are seeing and the ones we are unable to control.

I am unable to give you a list of port numbers that

could

be opened on the Optimus server, as these are generated dynamically as and when required.

To date we have not had any issues with our applications or servers in regards to MariaDB max connections or the need to flush-hosts from the database.

I presume that this message is only being displayed to ‘remote users’ and the hostnames / IP’s of their machines when they are running the ZTNA app / connector and is not happening on any of the local Optimus client machines?

This does seems to be an issue with how your ZTNA app is interfacing with the MariaDB database and requires it’s connections to be ‘flushed’ as they are either creating too many or not clearing their communication connections.

As I am sure you are aware, any from of increased load or reaching of maximum thresholds on the MariaDB database will have serious effects on the core Optimus application and could prevent the application running for

ALL

users if MariaDB stalls.

Vishaal A

(Partner) asked a question.

August 4, 2025 at 7:38 PM

ZPA RHEL9 App Connectors on Hyper-V

Hi all,

Due to the changes with ESXi, we have customers exploring migrations to Hyper-V

What are the supported configurations for Hyper-V using RHEL9 App connectors, if any.

What suggested alternatives could be used without deploying to Azure/AWS (customer servers are mostly on-prem).

ZPA - Forwarding

5 answers

970 views

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

a year ago

Hi Vishaal,

We do not currently provide any pre-built images of App Connector for Hyper-V.  We are tracking demand, so please let your PBM, or Account Teams know so they can assure the customers are tracked.  Demand is quite low currently.  Your current options are:

1) Customer installs RHEL8, or ideally RHEL9 and uses either our rpm-based installer or our docker container app conenctor

2) Customer installs any other linux distribution they are comfortable with and uses our docker container based app connector.

Mike

I have let our account team know we are interested in anything supported on Hyper-V.   Hopefully there is current consideration for pre-build images (app connectors, indexing server).

@Christian Dobol​ please make sure your account team has added you to the relevant Enhancement Request.  Product Management is actively tracking interest. RPM install is NOT supported on Rocky

and will cause supportability issues if you call in to TAC. Please be sure you're running our container on Docker or Podman if you're using any Linux distribution other than RH EL8 or RH EL9.

Anurag12345

(Customer) asked a question.

August 6, 2025 at 6:19 PM

'Username mismatched. Please try again' Error | ZPA Partner Tenant

We have a third service provider who has a Zscaler Tenant. My organization has another zscaler tenant. The third service provider has to access my Organization Internal resources. This the service provider can do by adding my organization tenant as partner tenant. Our organization has allowed access to connect from remote tenant on Zscaler Client Connector portal. Similarly third service provider has provided access to connect to any remote tenant. They are able to connect to a tenant of other organization.

However, we are facing issue when third service provider uses my organization id in partner tenant. We are receiving error '

Username mismatched. Please try again

'.

The user is able to login with same id if logged in as main tenant on same non-domain machine. On domain machine too with same user ID and password we are able to login as main id.

Let me know what we can do to resolve it?

Any input would be appreciated

as i am not able to find anything for above issue.

We have tried logging out other partner tenant ids too for the service provider user but still our tenant id could not be added.

We logged out the user from his main ID and logged in back to remove any cache kind of error, but still our organization id could not be used as tenant.

ZPA - Authentication

Please find the error screenshot.

Anurag12345

Hi Everyone,

Can use of older Zscaler Client Connector version can cause this issue?

Fileno

(Partner)

a year ago

After you have allowed that a 3rd party can login at your Tenant at ZCCP,  this users will need an IdP account at your domain and you will have to give permission in your ZPA, as you do for an internal users.

The ZPA Partner Tenant allows a 3rd party company access your Tenant, but you still need to grant permissions at your ZPA instance for this users that is accessing, and need to be an account from your IdP.

Normal RDP access to our dev team

at the same time secure bowser based RDP access to 3rd parties to the same VM(s)

For test purpose, place 1 RDP test Server in a New App Segment, Segment Group, etc, and then configure PRA, plus configure Access Policies. If properly configured  it should will work for users connecting through PRA Portal and also through ZCC. Suggest to separate this  RDP traffic in a specific App Segment.  Here PRA docs

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/privileged-remote-access-management

Short name on ZPA on Macs don't work

Hi I recentely moved our clients from FortiClient to ZPA and it's huge success. For all Windows clints we can access all internal resources without FQDN but for Mac clients they need to use the FQDN while on ZPA/WFH. Not a major issue but nice to fix this issue - Any idea how can we do this ? (When the Mac clints are in the office & ZPA will auto disable & no need to use FQDN)

ZPA - Admin Portal

3 answers

412 views

Top Rated Answers

konstantinos.betsis

(Partner)

a year ago

I general it's considered "safer" to allow users access based on the FQDN rather than the IP address since you are hiding your infrastructure details that way.

As mentioned above the steps to do that are simple:

Create application segments based on IP addresses. FQDNs and hostnames

Update the respective DNS search domains to include your own DNS zone names.

This way application segments will be reachable through all means, IP address, FQDN and hostname auto-populated with the domain through the OS DNS search function.

## Windows Autopilot with ZIA/ZPA

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000eB1hA0AS/windows-autopilot-with-ziazpa
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-09-15T03:55:20.000Z

ZIA - Authentication

Diode

(Customer) asked a question.

September 4, 2025 at 2:34 PM

Windows Autopilot with ZIA/ZPA

Hi we are planning to test Windows Auto Pilot deployment anything I need to know or do ? Appreciate any feedback

ZIA - Authentication

2 answers

524 views

Paddy_Ganti

(Employee)

a year ago

When planning to test Windows Autopilot deployment, here are key points to consider regarding authentication:

Azure AD Join

: Ensure that your devices are set up for Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) join, as this is a common requirement for Autopilot deployments.

User Authentication

: Choose between the self-deployment mode, which doesn’t require user credentials for initial enrollment, or the user-driven mode that requires users to authenticate with their Azure AD credentials.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

: Consider whether MFA will be required during the Autopilot process, as this may affect the user experience and the configuration setup.

Network Requirements

: Ensure devices have access to the internet to contact necessary authentication and Autopilot services.

Microsoft Endpoint Manager/Intune Configuration

: Configure your policies and profiles in Microsoft Endpoint Manager or Intune to facilitate a smooth authentication process during deployment.

Testing and validating these authentication aspects will help ensure a successful Autopilot deployment.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

10 months ago

## Split Horizon DNS

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000eTwRr0AK/split-horizon-dns
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-09-15T05:15:46.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZeroTrustNinja

(Customer) asked a question.

September 9, 2025 at 11:20 PM

Split Horizon DNS

We have *.example.com in ZPA as an app segment to forward all traffic for the entire domain (including subdomains *) to ZPA as we think everything for it is all private but we have many in that, for example, support.example.com, dev.example.com, uat.example.com and many more which has internal as well as public facing resolution and its too hard to find all that individually. Even if we find all individuals, how can we make sure which dns resolution users are requesting, private or public?? And how can we efficiently route that traffic?

6 answers

390 views

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

10 months ago

If you want to bypass ZPA for public facing applications, use Client forwarding policy, but we should have separate app segment for public facing applications.

IF you have App segment configured for *.

example.com

; ZPA receives the traffic destined for *.

example.com

and, based on its configuration, routes it to the App Connector. However, ZPA doesn't inherently know if the user's DNS resolution was private or public. It simply takes the traffic and tries to forward it to the App Connector, which is configured to access the internal resource. So public traffic will also try to go via ZPA.

ZeroTrustNinja

(Customer)

10 months ago

Does this mean Zscaler do not have a solution for this problem? I am sure we are not the first enterprise to have this scenario.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

10 months ago

I used to take the approach mentioned above because movement you try to access a URL, If App segment configured that URL or its wildcard will reach to ZPA.  App connector will route it through the reachable destination URL. ( Won't look at public or private. )

JSK27

(Partner)

10 months ago

Zscaler itself cannot distinguish between public and private DNS. This requires administrators to clearly identify and manage which URLs/domains are accessed internally.

For domains that have both public and private records, exceptions must be configured in the App Profile to ensure that they do not go through ZPA.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

10 months ago

Instead of PAC / APP profile exception you can with ZPA-Client forwarding configuration and bypass app segments with Public URLs which should not go via ZPA. That configuration will pick and go via ZIA.

JSK27

(Partner)

10 months ago

That’s correct. You can create exceptions through

Client Forwarding Policy – Bypass ZPA

(Partner)

9 months ago

I tested a similar setup in my lab, my difference is using port 80, I had no issue going to a web app by IP via the App Connector.

If you SSH to the app connector, can you validate that you can ping the IP of the application, or if there's a firewall in between, blocking ping, can you validate that you can issue a curl to the web application from the App Connector?

hriday.dhali

(Partner)

9 months ago

Hello Scott,

Thanks a lot for your reply.

We have almost thousands application, which is working perfectly, But few of the application have this type of strange behaviour.

Curl is also failed.

My query why telnet  working and how it's working  when ZPA ON? Which service, or kernal in app connector allowing telnet and blocking webservice.

Scott Daniels

(Partner)

9 months ago

The inability to ping or curl from the App Connector to the application points to something else interrupting the path.  Could be a physical or virtual firewall in between, or a local firewall on the server hosting the application.  That's where I would start for further troubleshooting on this issue.

As for your query on why telnet is working.  Due to the proxy architecture with the Zero Trust Exchange you are never directly connecting with Telnet to the destination application , but rather you are terminating at a Service Edge in the  Zero Trust Exchange.

I hope that is helpful.

CatV

(Customer) asked a question.

October 14, 2025 at 2:15 PM

Access Policy

What is the best way to build an access policy that keeps out users who are not part of a specific group?

ZPA - App Protection

2 answers

181 views

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

9 months ago

You can have generic policy for all users in the corporate. A minimal access policy.

And can build granular or detailed access for specific groups.

In rule you can have user or user group, so if you want to provide access to users who are not part of user group can accommodate within that policy itself.

manuel

(Customer)

9 months ago

Agree with Ramesh.

Additional note: best approach is IMHO always explicit allow listing because with block-listing you will always struggle keeping up to date. So create a group and include only the users you want to have access.

Zscaler Carrier-Grade NAT and Chromium Local Network Access

Hi there,

With the upcoming Chromium Local Network Access security feature release (

New permission prompt for Local Network Access | Blog | Chrome for Developers

), it seems that certain Zscaler configurations can cause that Internet hosts are resolved to Carrier-Grade NAT IP address range, which is considered local by this feature (see

Local Network Access

). This causes web application access issues, especially for scenarios where cross-origin iframes exist.

Is this known? If yes, what is the recommended configuration? It's foreseeable that this may cause significant impact, when Chrome gets this enabled by default in 142 (and Edge in 143).

Is this something used by other similar providers?

Thanks!

António

apmpinho

(Customer)

7 months ago

AFAIK, there are scenarios where exempting hosts through the available

allowedurls

policy is not possible. Google is working on a couple of policies to make this work better, with the first one more related with the CGN address space:

Enterprise policy to redefine network ranges as public for LNA [467085904] - Chromium

Enterprise policy to change the default inheritance of the local network access permission (LNA) [467417114] - Chromium

But until then, instead of staying in 141, it may be better to use the

LocalNetworkAccessRestrictionsTemporaryOptOut

policy. The same is true for Microsoft Edge, obviously.

LocalNetworkAccessRestrictionsTemporaryOptOu

t to true until we can set

as per that 1st feature request. I'm hoping this will be introduced before v146. However, it may still not work until the 2nd feature request for inheritance = automatic is created.

## ZScaler ZPA App Connectors deployment and issues

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000l70bQ0AQ/zscaler-zpa-app-connectors-deployment-and-issues
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-12-10T10:18:14.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - App Protection

zscaler_cisco

(Customer) asked a question.

November 28, 2025 at 1:43 PM

ZScaler ZPA App Connectors deployment and issues

I have very little experience with ZScaler, but here is my environment:

- HQ where all the users are located,

- Fully remote users,

- Data Center X,

- Azure environment,

- Internet access is coming out of Data Center X,

We deploy four App Connectors, two in Azure and two in Data Center X. The two

App Connectors have their own Internet access in Azure while the other two

App Connectors Data Center X use Internet in Data Center X. We have a VPN tunnel

between Data Center X and customer A Data Center Y. The way the network is setup is

that there is a 10G connections between HQ and Data Center X, and express route

between Data Center X and Azure. There is a 5ms latency between HQ and Data Center

X, and 11ms between HQ and Azure (in order to get to Azure from HQ, traffic must

goes through Data Center X). So far so good, right?

Here are the problems:

#1: When a user in HQ needs to access an application locates in customer A Data

Center Y, I notice that it uses Azure App Connectors instead of Data Center X

App Connectors. WHY?

#2: In our Azure App Connectors, I see one App Connector has five times more usage

(application tunnel) than the other App Connector. WHY? How do I go about load

balancing between these two Azure App Connectors?

ZPA - App Protection

4 answers

465 views

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

8 months ago

The ZPA selection mechanism operates on a principle of finding the closest and healthiest App Connector that can reach the requested application. Application-to-App Connector Group Association.

Private applications are configured within Application Segments in the ZPA Admin Portal.Each Application Segment is associated with one or more App Connector Groups. An App Connector must belong to an App Connector Group that is associated with the application it needs to reach.

When a user requests access to an application (via Zscaler Client Connector or Browser Access), the ZPA cloud service determines which App Connector to use. ZPA constantly monitors the latency between the ZPA Public Service Edge (the cloud component the user connects to) and all associated App Connectors. The ZPA cloud selects the closest App Connector given the user's location and the App Connector-to-application latency. This ensures that user traffic is forwarded to the App Connector that provides the quickest path to the desired private application.

If multiple App Connectors in an associated group can reach the application with similar, acceptable latency, ZPA uses them for load distribution and high availability. Zscaler recommends deploying multiple App Connectors (ideally in pairs) within an App Connector Group for redundancy and better scaling, rather than scaling up a single connector. This horizontal scaling allows for minimal disruption during failures or software updates.

rajk5

(Employee)

8 months ago

@David Tran​

For everyone else, I have tried to put it in a diagram.

For #1:

A few things come to mind:

Have you mapped the server groups correctly with your App segments? If you have mapped all app connectors with your app segment, and ZPA auto selection is not working as expected, then you can start being more specific in your configuration. Only map the server group that contains App connectors from DC-X with the app segment for applications hosted in DC-Y.

Usually ZPA auto selection works fine for most customers. But this is dependent on lots of variables, which might not be in Zscaler or customer control. All app connectors are supposed to report back with the health of ZPA applications back to the ZPA cloud. They all follow their own egress to send health data to their nearest ZPA broker. A delay in this path can cause delay in the health information, which can cause issues and appropriate app connector might not get selected. This is not the only reason.

You should also check if you have done any additional traffic steering in your ZPA access Policies. You may select all app connector in your app segment, and further restrict that in your ZPA access policy as to which app connector group it is supposed to use to serve those applications.

This can be another solution you can use. In the Access policy which is supposed to allow access to application in DC-Y, select traffic steering as App connector group X.

So you have 2 options:

With the app segment for applications hosted in DC-Y, only map the server group that has App connectors from DC-X

In the Access Policy to allow access for application in DC-Y, use "Traffic Steering" and choose the App connector group "Group X"

For #2:

You cannot do manual load balancing between the two app connectors. ZPA performs traffic distribution between configured app connectors, but it doesn't have to be equally distributed between the two.

This needs further diagnosis with the help of ZPA diagnostics logs, please open a support ticket to get it investigated.

avshch,

After creating a Machine Provisioning Key, you assign the Machine Token to use within the App Profile.  Create Access Policy for Machine Tunnel (Client Type).   From the Client Connector Portal, you can go to Enrolled Devices | Machine Tunnel to see active machine tunnels.

ritik.sh

Create a provisioning key.

Create an App Profile and link the provisioning key to that app profile by assigning machine token.

Use the policy token of that app profile as ZCC install parameter so that ZCC can discover the provisioning key and use that for machine authentication

skywalker

(Partner) asked a question.

December 22, 2025 at 9:36 PM

ZPA entra Auth fails

Hello , i have an issue related to Entra and ZPA integration , Customer of mine has only purchased ZPA . SO we tried to integrate ZPA and Entra and it didnot work . I opened a ZS case and they said for entra integration , we also need to integrate ZIA app in Enterprise applications in Entra . We did that . ZIA tenant is in zscaler.net and ZPA in zscalertwo.net . So I asked Zscaler to link these two as they are in different clouds . They linked both of them . Now on ZCC , when a use tries to login , it redirects to Entra . User put the username and it asks for MFA . Even MFA is Cisco Duo . it checks the cisco duo and it works fine at this stage . but then when it tries to download zscaler service it immediately throws an error - 'Unable to verify the SAML response from the IDP

Zscaler team checked Entra config and also IDP config on both ZIA and ZPA .it looks fine . I checked the timezones are also OK ..

Even the customer also tried to reinstall ZCC . Can anyone suggest if they faced any similar issue ?

ZPA - Authentication

1 answer

254 views

Paddy_Ganti

(Employee)

6 months ago

ZPA Entra ID Integration Requirements

Based on your question about ZPA and Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) integration failing, it sounds like you've encountered a common licensing requirement that's not immediately obvious.

Direct Answer

You need ZIA (Zscaler Internet Access) licensing in addition to ZPA for full Entra ID integration. This is because the authentication flow for ZPA with Entra ID requires internet-bound traffic to reach Microsoft's authentication endpoints, which needs to be processed through ZIA for proper security and policy enforcement.

Why ZIA is Required for ZPA + Entra ID

The authentication flow works as follows:

User attempts to access ZPA application

ZPA redirects to Entra ID for authentication

Entra ID authentication requires internet access to Microsoft endpoints

ZIA inspects and secures this authentication traffic

After successful auth, user gets access to ZPA applications

Without ZIA, the authentication requests to Entra ID may fail due to:

Lack of proper SSL inspection and certificate handling

Missing security policies for Microsoft endpoints

Inability to handle the OAuth/SAML flows properly

Configuration Overview

1. ZIA Configuration

- Configure Microsoft Office 365 app in ZIA

- Enable SSL inspection for Microsoft authentication endpoints

- Create URL filtering exceptions for:

login.microsoftonline.com

graph.microsoft.com

- Other Microsoft auth endpoints

2. ZPA Configuration

- Set up SAML IdP configuration for Entra ID

- Configure user attribute mappings

- Set up SCIM provisioning if needed

Alternative Solutions

If additional ZIA licensing is not feasible:

Option 1: Browser Access (Clientless)

Use ZPA Browser Access for applications that support it

This bypasses the need for full ZCC client authentication flows

Option 2: Certificate-Based Authentication

Configure certificate-based authentication instead of Entra ID

Deploy certificates to devices for ZPA authentication

Option 3: Local SAML IdP

Use an on-premises SAML provider (like ADFS)

This may work without ZIA depending on your network configuration

Relevant Documentation

ZPA SAML Configuration:

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-saml-sso

Office 365 Integration Guide:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/office-365-configuration

ZPA Authentication Methods:

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-authentication

Important Considerations

Licensing Discussion

Discuss with your Zscaler account team about ZIA licensing options

There may be specific bundles or reduced licensing for authentication-only use cases

Consider the security benefits of having both ZIA and ZPA

Best Practices

Always test authentication flows in a lab environment first

Ensure proper certificate trust chains are established

Monitor authentication logs during initial deployment

Have fallback authentication methods configured

Support Escalation

Since you already have an open case with Zscaler support, ask them specifically about:

Minimum ZIA licensing requirements for Entra ID integration

Alternative authentication methods for ZPA-only deployments

Timeline and cost implications for adding ZIA

Next Steps

Confirm licensing requirements with your Zscaler account team

Evaluate alternative authentication methods if ZIA is not immediately available

Plan phased deployment - ZPA with certificates first, then migrate to Entra ID once ZIA is available

Update your customer on the additional licensing requirement and options

## Browser isolation/chrome browser profiles control

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000oiHLJ0A2/browser-isolationchrome-browser-profiles-control
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-02-26T21:17:22.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Browser Isolation

avshch

(Customer) asked a question.

February 3, 2026 at 11:51 PM

Browser isolation/chrome browser profiles control

Is there a way to block/lock chrome profiles with Browser Isolation?

If not possible with Browser Isolation, what are the other available methods with Zscaler?

Thanks,

ZIA - Browser Isolation

3 answers

281 views

mahantr

likes this.

EalfaroZ34763

(Employee)

5 months ago

Hi Avshch,

Short answer: No —

Browser Isolation

controls user interaction in the isolated session (copy/paste, file transfer, printing, text input) but does not manage or lock local

Chrome profiles

. It’s not a profile-management tool.

If you need to enforce which Chrome is allowed, use these Zscaler methods:

ZPA Browser Access + Chrome posture profiles: Allow access only when users are on a managed Chrome Enterprise browser that meets your posture criteria; block when posture fails.(

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-access-policies

)(

https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-chrome-posture-profiles

ZCC Device Posture (ZIA/ZPA): Apply trust levels and policies based on device posture; use higher trust to allow, lower trust to isolate or block. (

https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/about-zia-posture-profiles

Some limitations:

Zscaler does not lock or select local Chrome profiles; it enforces access based on Chrome Enterprise posture signals, not a specific profile identifier. Use Google Admin policies (force sign-in/managed accounts) for profile lockdown, and pair with the ZPA posture gate above.

## ZPA, DNS Suffix and ZIA URL Issue

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000pBHgI0AW/zpa-dns-suffix-and-zia-url-issue
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-03-19T15:08:09.000Z

ZIA - URL Filtering

syntax22

(Partner) asked a question.

Edited March 18, 2026 at 12:27 PM

ZPA, DNS Suffix and ZIA URL Issue

Evening,

We forward ZPA traffic through ZIA for inspection. End users dont add the full FQDN for internal apps, so we added a DNS suffix which appears correctly on the client side.

Traffic flows through and when it hits ZIA, we got the internal APP URL classification as miscellaneous with browser isolation.

Created a global whitelist, added the internal suffix and expected that to bypass the URL filter,. This works fine if the user adds the full FQDN, but if they dont, it gets matched by ZPA based on the suffix / FQDN, but in ZIA it doesnt match the global whitelist for URL.

Example:

Site = testsite.internal.test.net

ZPA matches a wildcard currently on anything *.internal.test.net

Suffix added is internal.test.net

Globalwhitelist includes .internal.test.net

End user puts in testsite in their browser

ZPA matches the wildcard, forwards to ZIA, but it doesnt match the whitelist

If user enters testsite.internal.test.net it matches all the way through

Any ideas? We cant put individual exceptions in or match keywords as there is a huge amount of apps with non standard naming

/EDIT With Answer/

This is expected behaviour. The suffix is not inserted into the browser, so ZIA does not see the FQDN. We ended up modifying the misc category to not use browser isolation.

It would be quite nice if Zscaler had the option to not do URL filtering for ZPA segments though

ZIA - URL Filtering

## Chrome Enterprise Device Trust integration with Zscaler

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000rwnFP0AY/chrome-enterprise-device-trust-integration-with-zscaler
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-04-29T20:45:27.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Admin Portal

avshch

(Customer) asked a question.

March 31, 2026 at 2:54 PM

Chrome Enterprise Device Trust integration with Zscaler

We are attempting to setup Chrome Enterprise Device Trust integration with Zscaler as per guide available at https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13570263?hl=en

It appears we don't have "Chrome Enterprise Browser" under "Configuration & Control" at ZPA Administration menu.

According to the guide this feature is available for all licensed editions of Zscaler Private Access.

Any feedback is appriciated.

Thanks,

ZPA - Admin Portal

1 answer

183 views

Pablo Guzman

(Employee)

3 months ago

Likely cause: the

Chrome Enterprise Browser integration

UI is gated by feature flags on your ZPA tenant, not by license alone. When the flags aren’t enabled, the menu item won’t appear, even though the feature is supported across editions.

What to check/do:

Verify the current location: in recent builds it lives under

Policies > Access Control > Clientless > Browser Extension > Settings

, not a standalone item in “Configuration & Control.”

Confirm your

admin role/permissions

allow Access Policy and Clientless settings.

Ask Zscaler your TAM to enable these feature flags on your tenant

After enablement, you can configure the

Connector settings

in ZPA and then add the

Zscaler connector in Google Admin

as per the deployment guide.

Notes:

Diagnostics for this integration appear under

Logs > Insights > Diagnostics

(select Chrome Enterprise Browser) and may be in

limited availability

depending on tenant rollout.

ZPA detects a managed browser via the

X-Device-Trust

header from Chrome; ensure your managed Chrome policies are applied.

The integration is GA for

Browser Access

use cases; see the 2025 release notes for context.

## ZPA Not Authenticated State Causes System Slowness on Windows 11 Pro,25H2

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000sNmhg0AC/zpa-not-authenticated-state-causes-system-slowness-on-windows-11-pro25h2
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-05-13T12:47:25.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Posture

Tuhin Patra

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited April 8, 2026 at 9:32 AM

ZPA Not Authenticated State Causes System Slowness on Windows 11 Pro,25H2

An intermittent issue is observed on an HP EliteBook Ultra G1i 14‑inch Notebook (Next Gen AI PC – IDS Base Model) running Windows 11, with Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8.0.156, where the system becomes slow or unresponsive only when Zscaler is installed and running in a “ZPA Not Authenticated” state with the Network Type marked as Off Trusted Network. There is no issue when ZPA is connected or when Zscaler is fully disabled. The issue occurs on public/open Wi‑Fi when ZPA authentication does not initiate, affecting Outlook desktop, Microsoft 365 apps, and Windows UI elements (Taskbar, Search). Disabling and re‑enabling Wi‑Fi immediately restores apps. The system works normally on corporate LAN/Wi‑Fi with ZPA disabled.

ZIA - Posture

4 answers

429 views

Richard Hesselbach

(Employee)

3 months ago

What the symptom pattern strongly suggests

Because the slowness happens only when Client Connector is running and ZPA is “Not Authenticated” (and Network Type = Off Trusted Network), the most likely root causes fall into a few buckets:

Network stack stall caused by a “half-on” ZPA posture

ZPA is enabled, Windows sees the Wi‑Fi as untrusted, but ZPA authentication/tunnel establishment does not start/complete.

That can leave Windows and apps waiting on network calls (DNS, proxy/WPAD, TLS, identity, captive portal detection) that are being intercepted/filtered but not successfully satisfied.

Public Wi‑Fi factors: captive portal / blocked flows

Public/open Wi‑Fi often blocks or intercepts flows until a portal is completed.

If required Zscaler auth/bootstrap endpoints aren’t reachable yet, the client may repeatedly attempt and time out, while apps (Outlook/M365) keep retrying in the background—sometimes causing UI hangs if core services are waiting on network responses.

DNS / WPAD / proxy discovery loops

Outlook/M365 and Windows shell can become sluggish when:

DNS resolution is slow or repeatedly failing,

WPAD auto-detection is timing out,

proxy settings are being applied but the proxy path isn’t usable in this “Not Authenticated” state.

Driver / filter interaction

Client Connector installs network filter components. In a failure mode, you can see high latency in networking calls system-wide, which “feels” like the whole machine is slow (taskbar/search included) because many UI elements call network-backed services.

The fact that toggling Wi‑Fi fixes it immediately is a key clue: it resets the interface, captive portal detection, DNS state, and any stuck socket/proxy discovery attempts.

Fast containment / mitigation you can try (to keep users productive)

Complete/trigger captive portal sign-in first

On public Wi‑Fi, open a browser to

http://neverssl.com

(or any HTTP site) to force the portal.

After portal completion, see whether ZPA authentication starts normally.

Temporarily disable WPAD

Windows: Settings → Network & Internet → Proxy → Automatically detect settings = Off

This reduces “proxy auto discovery” delays that can freeze app startup/login on unstable Wi‑Fi.

Force a clean network state without full Wi‑Fi toggle

Try

ipconfig /flushdns

(admin not always required)

Or disable/enable the adapter (equivalent to the user workaround).

If policy allows, set a user workflow

“If ZPA shows Not Authenticated on public Wi‑Fi: complete captive portal → then reconnect ZPA / restart Client Connector.”

What to collect (so support/engineering can pinpoint it)

A. Client Connector logs around the event

Collect Client Connector Support Bundle while the machine is in the bad state (or immediately after reproduction).

Note timestamps and capture:

ZPA status transitions (Connected → Not Authenticated)

Any errors about authentication, broker reachability, certs, or posture.

B. Windows network/proxy/DNS state (during “bad” state)

Have the user capture outputs when slowness is happening:

ipconfig /all

netsh winhttp show proxy

reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" /v AutoConfigURL

Windows Proxy settings screenshot

Whether a captive portal is present and completed

C. Performance traces (to prove “system slow” is network-call blocking)

Task Manager:

CPU usage of Zscaler processes and Service Host: Network Service

Any process pegging CPU or showing “Not Responding” threads

Optional but very useful:

Windows Performance Recorder (WPR) trace during the stall (Networking + CPU)

This can show if threads are blocked on DNS/proxy/network APIs.

Targeted things to test (to isolate the trigger)

TestExpected outcomeWhat it tells youPublic Wi‑Fi with captive portal completed first, then start Client ConnectorIf issue disappearsCaptive portal / blocked bootstrap endpoints are the triggerSame Wi‑Fi but set Windows Proxy “Auto-detect” OffIf issue improvesWPAD/proxy discovery timeouts are contributingTry a different public hotspot (phone tether vs café Wi‑Fi)If only some networks trigger itNetwork filtering/portal behavior is the triggerRepro on same laptop with ZPA disabled but ZIA enabled (if applicable)Helps isolate moduleConfirms whether the stall is specific to ZPA componentUpdate Client Connector to a newer GA build (if available in your org)If fixedPoints to a client bug fixed post‑4.8.0.156

Sharing for visibility in case others face similar behaviour.
