## CyberArk replacement

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000snWzV0AU/cyberark-replacement
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-05-09T00:07:23.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

PankajM55

(Customer) asked a question.

April 14, 2026 at 4:08 PM

CyberArk replacement

Can Zscaler replace CyberArk App Gateway (reverse proxy) for access to internal web apps, while we still use CyberArk SWS just for session recording?

ZPA - Privileged Remote Access

1 answer

233 views

Eric N.

(Employee)

2 months ago

The answer depends on your specific use cases.

Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) can typically replace the reverse-proxy “publish internal web apps” function of CyberArk App Gateway for user access to internal web applications.

I am  a little confused by the question. One cannot “use CyberArk SWS just for session recording”, because SWS (AIM/SWS) is for secret retrieval and provides audit logs of secret requests, not interactive web session recording.

Zscaler already offers session recording today for privileged access to private apps via Privileged Remote Access (PRA) for RDP/SSH/VNC, but not for general web sessions to private web apps (at least not yet). PRA session recording is positioned for admin workflows and includes audit controls like watermarking, clipboard/file transfer controls, etc

Web App Gateway use case

ZPA provides zero-trust access to internal web apps without inbound exposure, using identity-based policy and application segmentation. It also provides full logging of who connected to what from where and when.

ZPA Browser Access and Privileged Remote Access provides access to internal applications without exposing your public IP addresses as VPNs and VDI solutions do.

Combining Browser Access with Browser Isolation allows security engineers to tightly control how users interact with a web application, for example, blocking copy and paste, blocking printing, or watermarking the viewed pages.

## ZIA/ZPA sandbox

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000uMT0A0AW/ziazpa-sandbox
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-05-13T14:02:16.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

ajayg1567

(Customer) asked a question.

May 10, 2026 at 1:03 PM

ZIA/ZPA sandbox

looking to set up cloud sandbox for zpa and zia. can anyone et me know steps

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

3 answers

412 views

Allen Geiser

(Employee)

3 months ago

Setting up a cloud sandbox for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) involves configuring the inspection policies in ZIA and then integrating those capabilities into your ZPA workflows (typically via Source IP Anchoring or Privileged Remote Access).

Below are the steps to set up and integrate the two:

1. ZIA Sandbox Setup (Primary)

The Sandbox lives natively in ZIA to inspect files for malware.

Enable SSL Inspection: This is a critical prerequisite. The Sandbox cannot inspect encrypted traffic (HTTPS) unless SSL Inspection is enabled for those categories/URLs.

Configure Malware Protection: Go to Policies > Cybersecurity > Malware Protection and ensure Inbound/Outbound Traffic Inspection is enabled.

Define Sandbox Rules: Navigate to Policies > Cybersecurity > Sandbox.

Add a rule and choose your action:

Quarantine: Holds the file until a full analysis is complete (best for preventing "Patient 0").

Allow and Scan: Delivers the file immediately but scans it in the background for retrospective reporting.

AI Instant Verdict: Enable this toggle within the rule to allow machine learning to provide real-time risk assessment.

2. ZPA Integration

To apply Sandbox protection to your private applications, you must route that traffic through ZIA.

For Private Applications (SIPA):

In the ZPA Portal, go to Resource Management > Application Segments.

Enable Source IP Anchoring (SIPA) on the specific App Segment you want to protect.

In the ZIA Portal, create a Sandbox rule and select that specific App Segment as a criterion. This forces traffic to the private app to be inspected by the ZIA Sandbox.

For Privileged Remote Access (PRA):

If you use Clientless/PRA for file transfers, go to the ZPA portal: Policies > Access Control > Clientless > Sandbox Integration.

Enter your ZIA Cloud Name, API Key, and Admin Credentials.

This allows you to select the "Inspect" option for file transfers during a PRA session.

3. Verification

Test Downloads: Use a safe test file (like the EICAR test file) to ensure the Sandbox triggers as expected based on your "Quarantine" or "Allow" settings.

Monitor Logs: Check the Web Insights or Sandbox Insights in the ZIA dashboard to see file verdicts and analysis reports.

## ZPA route audit logs

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000uVpDq0AK/zpa-route-audit-logs
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-05-12T19:46:11.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - Logging

gayatri.debnath

(Partner) asked a question.

May 12, 2026 at 5:49 PM

ZPA route audit logs

Team, I am trying to find the audit logs for app connector routes that were changed a week ago. We lost all the routes and I am looking for the changes made.

Where can i find this?

ZPA - Logging

1 answer

227 views

Allen Geiser

(Employee)

2 months ago

In the Zscaler ecosystem, configuration changes for App Connectors—including route changes—are managed and logged within the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal, rather than the ZDX (Experience Center) portal.

While ZDX provides visibility into the performance and health of App Connectors, it does not track administrative configuration changes (like route modifications) made to the ZPA infrastructure.

Where to find these logs (ZPA Portal)

To find the changes made a week ago, you must go to the ZPA Admin Portal:

Navigate to:

Administration

Admin Management

Audit Logs

Select Tab: Ensure you are on the Private Access tab.

Date Filter: Change the time range to "Custom" and select the window from one week ago.

Resource Type Filter: To find route-related changes, filter by:

App Connector Group (if the connector configuration was updated).

Application Segment (if routes/segments were deleted or changed).

Server Group (if the mapping to the connectors was modified).

What you can see in ZDX (Experience Center)

If you are looking in ZDX, you will only see:

ZDX Audit Logs: These only track changes made

within

ZDX (e.g., creating a new application probe or changing an alert rule).

App Connector Status: Under Infrastructure > App Connectors, you can see the health and connection status, but not the history of configuration edits.

Recommendation: If you suspect the routes were lost due to an administrative error, the ZPA Audit Logs are your only source of truth. Click the View (eye icon) next to any "Update" or "Delete" action to see the "Before" and "After" values, which will help you reconstruct the missing routes.

## Does ZPA support bidirectional UDP for a VDI display protocol (PCoIP UDP/4172)?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000xALmQ0AW/does-zpa-support-bidirectional-udp-for-a-vdi-display-protocol-pcoip-udp4172
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2026-06-27T11:45:59.000Z

ZPA - Forwarding

kyota

(Customer) asked a question.

June 24, 2026 at 12:43 PM

Does ZPA support bidirectional UDP for a VDI display protocol (PCoIP UDP/4172)?

Hello,

We are planning to migrate the remote-access path for a Horizon-based VDI environment from a traditional VPN to ZTNA (Zscaler ZPA), and I'd like to confirm whether PCoIP can work over ZPA.

Architecture (simplified / anonymized):

Remote end-user device → VDI gateway → virtual desktops.

The gateway is an F5 BIG-IP APM acting as a PCoIP proxy / secure gateway. The client connects to a single gateway VIP.

Connection brokering to the Horizon Connection Servers is HTTPS/TCP 443 only (PCoIP does not traverse the Connection Servers).

PCoIP display traffic uses UDP/4172 and is relayed by the gateway between client and desktop. (Blast Extreme UDP/8443 is also provisioned but not currently used.)

The client always initiates the session. Once established, display data flows from the server side back to the client over UDP/4172, so traffic on 4172 is bidirectional.

My understanding is that ZTNA/ZPA is primarily designed around client-initiated TCP connections, and UDP is connectionless (no handshake to anchor a "client-initiated" session).

Questions:

Does ZPA support UDP application traffic such as PCoIP UDP/4172 end-to-end, including the server→client return traffic within a client-initiated session?

Has anyone successfully run Horizon PCoIP through ZPA? Any required configuration, limitations, or MTU/performance considerations?

If PCoIP UDP is not fully supported, would Blast Extreme over TCP (443/8443) be the recommended, more ZTNA-friendly alternative?

Thanks in advance.

ZPA - Forwarding

1 answer

233 views

avshch

(Customer)

a month ago

PCoIP is supported with ZIA. We were able to configure Amazon AWS Workspace desktop client which does use PCoIP.

There are some posts in ref to other posts:
